PP14/3 holds alien registration applications for GABRIELE PROSTAMO and FRANCESCO PROSTAMO at Perth, CIRCA 1916-1920 -- thirty years earlier than anything this archive holds in Australia, and in the wrong state. Unread.

source: NAA NameSearch — the complete POLISTENA set, fifty items, separated from the town of the same name
scope: NameSearch, all record categories, on POLISTENA, read out in full at 200 to a page.
result: FIFTY ITEMS, AND THE FIRST THING TO DO WITH THEM IS SPLIT THEM IN TWO. POLISTENA IS A COMUNE IN REGGIO CALABRIA AS WELL AS A SURNAME, and NameSearch does not know the difference: four A714 naturalisations come back for men named OLIMPIO, MARFEA, FOGLIADORO and PALESTRI whose PLACE OF BIRTH is Polistena, and three A7919 prisoner-of-war records for SAVARESE, ROSSI and BOTTIGLIERI, born there and captured in Africa. THIS ARCHIVE'S POLISTENA ARE FROM SCILLA, seventy kilometres away. Seven of the fifty are the town, not the family. THREE HITS THAT MATTER. ONE. J25 1971/3900, Brisbane, 1953-1971: «ARENA, ROCCO; WIFE ANGELINA [OR ANGELA] [NEE POLISTENA]». Row 80 of the work list says their marriage «is not documented anywhere in this archive». HERE IS A COMMONWEALTH FILE THAT NAMES THEM AS HUSBAND AND WIFE AND GIVES HER MAIDEN NAME. It does not date the marriage; it proves it and it names the file that may. Not yet examined, held at Brisbane. TWO. BP9/3, ITALIAN POLISTENA G: «Polistena, GIOVANNI BORN 1883 - arrived in BRISBANE on the ORMONDE on 21 FEBRUARY 1928». This archive's GIOVANNI POLISTENA was born at Scilla in 1883, act 206, and is already documented sailing from PALERMO to NEW ORLEANS on the LIGURIA in February 1908, on the line immediately after Michele Donato. A SECOND MIGRATION, TWENTY YEARS LATER AND TO THE OTHER SIDE OF THE WORLD, would explain how this family reached Queensland at all. The year of birth matches exactly and the port is the right one. IT IS A CANDIDATE AND NOT A FINDING: the entry carries no parents and no birthplace. The test is the item itself, or a Queensland record placing him there in the 1930s. THREE. TWO MORE DONATO-POLISTENA MARRIAGES, IN QUEENSLAND THIS TIME. J25 1967/9873: «Polistena, Giuseppe; wife MARIA MADDALENA [NEE DONATO]». J25 1970/3023: «DONATO, CONCETTA [NEE POLISTENA]». With the four already found in the Scilla death index, that is SIX marriages between these two families across two countries and two generations. THE REST OF THE FAMILY-PLAUSIBLE ITEMS, written out so nobody pays for this again. SP908/1 (Sydney aliens): Maria Angela Polistena [nee Lipari], NEPTUNIA 24 May 1954; Annunziata Lipari also known as Polistena, ROMA 26 Nov 1964; Domenico Polistena, SURRIENTO 20 July 1950; Vincenzo Polistena, SURRIENTO 20 July 1950; Maria Carmela Polistena [nee Multari], aircraft 31 Aug 1963; Annunziato, Salvatore and Antonino Polistena, all aircraft 31 Aug 1963; Bellardina Polistena, SYDNEY 22 June 1957; Maria Vincenza Polistena, ROMA 26 Nov 1964. source: NAA NameSearch — the complete MELLUSO set, seventeen items
scope: NameSearch, all record categories, on MELLUSO, written out in full. Queensland's own index returns exactly ONE Melluso registration, so this archive had Gregorio Melluso with no siblings and no children recorded anywhere in Australia.
result: SEVENTEEN ITEMS, AND TWO OF THEM NAME A HUSBAND THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE. J25 1962/5930, Brisbane, 1952-1966: «PROSTAMO, DOMENICO FRANCESCO; WIFE ASSUNTE MARIA [NEE MELLUSO]». That is MARIA ASSUNTA MELLUSO, born about 1936 to Gregorio Melluso and Carmela Maria Borello, buried at Mount Gravatt in 1991 -- «the first Prostamo ever found in the Queensland index, and she was born a Melluso». HER HUSBAND'S NAME IS DOMENICO FRANCESCO PROSTAMO, and this is the first record of him. J25 1972/23086, Brisbane, 1959-1974: «MELLUSO, GREGORIO; WIFE CARMELA; AND CHILDREN GIUSEPPE, MARIA [SURNAME PROSTAMO]». Gregorio's own household, which Queensland's index could not show. «Wife Carmela» is Carmela Maria Borello. THE BRACKET IS AMBIGUOUS AND MUST NOT BE READ PAST: a daughter Maria carrying the surname Prostamo is simply Maria Assunta married; a SON Giuseppe carrying it is not, and would mean Carmela brought Prostamo children into the marriage. THE FILE TITLE IS A FINDING AID. Opening it would settle which, and it is «not yet examined». THE REST, WRITTEN OUT. SP1122/1 N1957/47306: Melluso, Rocco -- Italian migrant naturalisation file, Sydney, 1957-1963, «open with exception». MP1103/1 and MP1103/2, PWI49751: PRISONER OF WAR/INTERNEE MELLUSO, CARMELO, born 19 APRIL 1919, Italian, Melbourne -- a prisoner of war shipped to Australia, not a resident interned, and no evidence connects him here. BP289/1 001102370: Melluso, Giuseppe, arrived 29 February 1968 at Fremantle aboard GALILEO, file held at BRISBANE. A12038 995: PETRONIO-MELLUSO Felicia, born 25 September 1925. J25 1970/5204: PALMIERI, Antonio [born 1927]; wife VINCENZA [NEE MELLUSO] [born 1943]. C321 N1973/050286: Melluso, Carmela, Sydney. A9111 1981/1284: MELLUSO, Leonardo. B44 V1986/23418: Melluso, V, Melbourne. AND FIVE MELLUSO WOMEN ARE CATALOGUED UNDER MARRIED NAMES: Lucia DI BIASI «also known as Melluso»; Nicolina PAONE «also known as Melluso»; Domenica MELLUSO «also known as Patamia»; Vincenza MILETO «also known as Melluso»; and ORIANA (nee MELLUSO) Vicenta. THE SAME LESSON THE 1908 Scilla death index taught about Serafina Arlotta, in a different archive on the other side of the world: A MARRIED WOMAN IS INDEXED UNDER WHICHEVER NAME THE CLERK HAD, and a sweep that only reads the maiden surname column will miss her. Here the catalogue happens to carry both.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 28 and the annual Tavola, read in full
scope: Giovanni Arlotta x Maria Costa's marriage — the act that would settle an eleven-year conflict in his age and decide whether the Domenico Arlotta generation belongs to this family. Found from the annual Tavola after 1829 was cleared and 1830 was not needed.
result: ACT 28 OF 1828, AND IT SETTLES MORE THAN IT WAS ASKED TO. Scilla, 30 AUGUST 1828: GIOVANNI ARLOTTA, DI ANNI VENTOTTO, marinaro, FIGLIO DI FU DOMENICO ARLOTTA E DI ANNA BARBARO; and MARIA COSTA, D'ANNI VENTISEI, FIGLIA DI ROCCO DI COSTA, marinaro, E DI PASQUALINA IDONE. Banns posted Sunday 3 August; church wedding 7 SEPTEMBER 1828 before D. Domenico Zanghi and Bruno Ingrigneri. THE BRIDE'S PARENTS ATTENDED AND CONSENTED IN PERSON -- so Rocco Costa and Pasqualina Idone were both alive and in the room. DOMENICO ARLOTTA IS CONFIRMED AND DATED. He is «FU Domenico» here, so DEAD BEFORE 30 AUGUST 1828, twenty-six years tighter than the «before April 1854» this archive carried -- and the generation is not dislodged, which was the real risk. THREE NEW PEOPLE: ANNA BARBARO, Giovanni's mother; ROCCO COSTA and PASQUALINA IDONE, Maria's parents. All three alive in 1828, none in the family tree. AND IT BREAKS TWO AGES, ONE OF THEM WRITTEN BY ME THIS MORNING. Giovanni Arlotta is TWENTY-EIGHT here (b. c. 1800), FORTY on his daughter's birth act of 1830, and SEVENTY-FIVE on his grandson's of 1854 -- three of his own declarations spanning twenty-one years. The marriage act is preferred. Twenty-eight in 1828 is thirty in 1830, and «trenta» written or read as «quaranta» is ordinary; the 1854 «settantacinque» is not, and stays open as either a badly wrong age or a second Giovanni Arlotta son of a late Domenico. MARIA COSTA is TWENTY-SIX here (b. c. 1802) and this archive entered her as «c. 1807» a few hours earlier off the 1830 act. CORRECTED, WITH THE OLD FIGURE LEFT ON THE RECORD. A CANDIDATE WITHDRAWN BY THE SAME ACT. A DOMENICO COSTA, commerciante, forty-six, witnessed Serafina's registration in 1830 and was recorded here as a candidate for Maria Costa's father, graded «candidate» precisely so it could be withdrawn. HER FATHER WAS ROCCO. That is what the grade was for. AND THE TAVOLA CLOSED ANOTHER ROW FOR FREE. The 1828 annual index names BOTH SPOUSES' PARENTS, and its FIRST entry is «ARENA ANTONIO e DE LUCA SERAFINA -- ORAZIO e MORABITO LETTERIA / FILIPPO e ALFONZETTI ANNA -- 10 Ag.o 1828 -- atto 26». That is the OTHER Antonio Arena married to a Serafina, the collision guarded this morning; his parents are ORAZIO ARENA and LETTERIA MORABITO, which is where that family's Orazio comes from. 1829's Tavola opens at B with no A section at all, so neither surname married that year.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1851 Tavola annuale, entry 1, against the 1828 convention
scope: A direct test of a correction graded «inferred» that morning: were Filippo Arena, Domenica Costa, Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa alive when their children married in February 1851? The processetti bundle held no death act for any of them, which is an argument from absence.
result: CONFIRMED, AND BY A POSITIVE READING. Container LD6brxB, 96 images; the 1851 Tavola runs images 88-96 and ENTRY 1 IS «ARENA FRANCESCO e ARLOTTA SERAFINA», Scilla. Its parents column reads «FILIPPO, e COSTA DOMENICA» and «GIOVANNI e COSTA MARIA» -- both exactly right, and NEITHER CARRIES «FU». WHY THAT IS EVIDENCE AND NOT SILENCE. The same series marks the dead: the 1828 Tavola writes Giovanni Arlotta as son of «FU Dom.co e Barbaro Anna» -- father dead, mother living -- and «fu» appears on THIS PAGE of 1851 in other entries, including entry 4. The convention is in use locally and it is not applied to our four. THEY WERE ALL FOUR ALIVE IN FEBRUARY 1851. The morning's correction moves from «inferred» to «documented». AND THE INSTRUMENT IS BETTER THAN THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN TREATING IT. A Scilla marriage Tavola carries Num. d'ordine | Sposi | Patria | PROFESSIONE | GENITORI | Giorno della Celebrazione. One index opening therefore gives four parents AND dates the life status of all four, without opening an act. Every year of the restaurazione series will do this. ONE CAUTION FOR WHOEVER USES IT. The date column is the CHURCH celebration, not the civil act -- in 1828 the Tavola says 7 September where the civil promise was 30 August. An act number and a Tavola date will disagree by days or weeks and neither is wrong. AND THE ROWS ARE NOT CLEANLY ALIGNED: in 1851 the parents are written slightly above their own line and interleave with the neighbouring entry, so a parent pair must be matched to a spouse BY NAME, not by height on the page. Entry 1's four lines were disentangled that way.

source: Antenati — Scilla marriage indexes 1810, 1811, 1812, 1818, 1819 swept for Filippo Arena
scope: FILIPPO ARENA x DOMENICA COSTA'S MARRIAGE, which is the only route left to GENERATION NINE on the Scilla side. He was twenty-five and she twenty-seven when their son Francesco was born on 25 November 1819, so they married about 1812-1819. Four volumes' indexes checked; two more have none.
result: TWO CLEAN NEGATIVES AND A COVERAGE MAP. 1819 (container 0AJEJ8b, 79 images, Tavola at 75-79): alphabetised by SURNAME. Its A section holds ONE entry -- «Abbate Grazia e Capitano Giovanna», 8 Febraro. NO ARENA. 1818 (container LPaGar8, 43 images, Tavola at 41-43): alphabetised by the GROOM'S GIVEN NAME, exactly as this archive's cautions warn. FILIPPO THEREFORE SITS UNDER F, NOT A, and the F section is entries 10-13: Francesco Migliarino x Antonia Fulco (21 Gennaro), Francesco Polimeni x Clementina Perina (26 Gennaro), FILIPPO PIZZARELLO x Francesca Fava (27 Gennaro), Francesco La Valle x Nicola Florio (10 Aprile). NO FILIPPO ARENA. Searching the A section of 1818 would have produced a confident, complete and entirely false negative. 1817 (container 5K9P9J9, 43 images) HAS NO TAVOLA AT ALL -- the volume runs to act 41 and then blank forms. 1816 (container wQYJYDb, 45 images) LIKEWISE: acts to 42, then blanks, and the archivist's card reads VOLUME TARLATO, worm-eaten. SO THE UNREAD GROUND IS: 1816 and 1817, which cost a full act-by-act read of about forty openings apiece because there is no index to shortcut; and the NAPOLEONIC years 1809-1815, whose containers have not been bought (arks in scilla-arks.tsv). Scilla's registers begin in 1809, not 1816, so those years exist. ALL FOUR CONTAINERS ARE NOW SAVED so no later session pays for them again. EXTENDED THE SAME DAY INTO THE NAPOLEONIC FONDO, AND THREE MORE YEARS FALL. 1812 (container wX9PERp, 23 images, Tavola at 22-23): SEVENTEEN marriages, alphabetised by the GROOM'S GIVEN NAME. All seventeen read. NO FILIPPO ARENA. 1811 (container wl1gvZD, 19 images, Tavola at 18-19): same ordering. Its F section is Ferdinando di Franco, Francesco Arbitrio and Fulcantonio Bova. NO FILIPPO ARENA. 1810 (container LzjyVKj, 18 images, INDICE at 17-18): same ordering. Its F section is Filippo LAGANA, Francesco Vita, Francesco Martello, Francesco Zirilli and a Francesco Fa[va]. THERE IS A FILIPPO AND HE IS A LAGANA. NO FILIPPO ARENA. 1809 (container LD6vJel, 29 images) HAS NO TAVOLA -- acts to 27, then blank forms. SO THE MARRIAGE IS NOT IN 1810, 1811, 1812, 1818 OR 1819, and the unindexed years left are 1809, 1813-1814, 1815, 1816 and 1817. ALL NINE CONTAINERS ARE NOW SAVED. AND THE SWEEP PAID FOR ITSELF SIDEWAYS. The 1811 Tavola gives «GIOVANNI VILARDI x CANDIDA COSTA -- Gaetano ed Antonia Mellica / ROCCO e PASQUALINA IDONE». Rocco Costa and Pasqualina Idone are MARIA COSTA'S PARENTS, read three hours earlier off the 1828 marriage act. SO CANDIDA COSTA IS MARIA COSTA'S SISTER, married at Scilla in 1811 -- a generation-seven sibling found for free, in an index opened for somebody else. FOUR MORE SCILLA HOUSEHOLDS NOTED IN PASSING, none of them joined to this family: CARLO ARENA x EUGENIA GRAJA, whose daughter Giovanna married Giovanni La Mussa in January 1812; a «fu ANTONIA ARENA» named as a mother in 1812; NATALINA ARENA, a mother in 1811; and ANNA ARLOTTA, a mother in 1811. Carlo Arena is of roughly the right generation to be Filippo Arena's father and there is NOTHING WHATEVER to support that beyond the surname and the town -- recorded so the next session does not rediscover him and think it has found something.

source: NAA NameSearch — the complete MAZZA set, two hundred items, written out
scope: NameSearch, all record categories, on MAZZA, read out at 200 to a page. Swept once before and summarised; this pass exists to write the family-plausible items down.
result: TWO HUNDRED ITEMS. Four are prisoner-of-war files for men born in Italy and captured in Africa, unconnected. Of the rest, these are the ones that touch this family. ANDREA MAZZA IS DATED AT LAST. NAA: BP4/3, ITALIAN MAZZA A: «Mazza, Andrea - Nationality: Italian - NATURALISATION CERTIFICATE GRANTED 27 NOVEMBER 1934», held at Brisbane. Row 106 has him only as a TIMBER CUTTER AT CARDWELL on the 1959 electoral roll, a lead a roll could not settle. He was naturalised in Queensland TWENTY-FIVE YEARS EARLIER, and naturalisation of that period wanted about five years' residence, so he was in Australia by about 1929. He is not a post-war arrival and not a stranger passing through. IT STILL DOES NOT MAKE HIM A RELATIVE -- the certificate names no parents -- but it turns a single roll line into a man with two dates. AND MARIO MAZZA WITH HIM: BP4/3, ITALIAN MAZZA M, naturalisation certificate granted 11 NOVEMBER 1927. That fits the Mario Mazza who married Peppina Mazzaglia in Queensland in 1924 and whose son Rosario was born there in 1925. WHAT HAPPENED TO ROSARIO MAZZA AFTER THE CAMP. NAA: J1737, MAZZA R: «Mazza Rosario, CAS 15000 - CIVIL ALIENS CORPS (CAC)», Brisbane, 1944, ACCESS OPEN. The Civil Aliens Corps is the labour corps internees were released into, and this archive had his internment dossier (MP1103/1, Q8110) and nothing after it. A service number, CAS 15000, and a file. OTHER FAMILY-PLAUSIBLE ITEMS. A261 1948/625: «Applicant - MAZZA Rosario; Nominee - PAGLIARO Carmela; PAGLIARO Loretta Donna Maria» -- Rosario sponsoring two women into Australia in 1948. J25 1962/1887: «Mazza, Giuseppe, Sebastiano, Stefano and Graziella», Brisbane. J25 1970/5500: «Applicant: Mazza, SEBASTIANO; Nominee: Napoli, Mario and wife Maria [NEE COCO]» -- and a Maria Mazza married a Rosario COCO in Queensland in 1939, so the Coco are in this circle twice. J25 1966/11584: «Mazza, Angelo; wife Francesca [nee Strano]; and child Giovanni» -- Angelo Mazza and Francesca Strano are already in the Queensland death index as Giovanni Mazza's parents. J25 1951/10120 and B78 ITALIAN/MAZZA SERAFINO GIOVANNI: Serafino Giovanni Mazza, arrived BRISBANE per SYDNEY 3 April 1952. BP145/1: Antonio Mazza, born 25 January 1935, arrived CAIRNS on the AURELIA, May 1956. BP25/1 ITALIAN SPATARO G: «Spataro [nee Mazza], Grazia», arrived Sydney on the Sebastiano Caboto 9 February 1951. A FINDING AID WORTH KNOWING: NAA BP628/5, «Name Index and registration cards for internees dossiers QUEENSLAND - MACAUDO to MYSLIM», 1939-1962, Brisbane, OPEN. That is the index to the Queensland internee dossiers, and MAZZA falls inside its range. TWO GUARDS. A12508 31/3204 is a DIFFERENT ROSARIO MAZZA, born 1 FEBRUARY 1877, arriving Melbourne per VIMINALE on 10 July 1939 -- twenty-two years older than this archive's Rosario and landing at the wrong port in the same decade. A12508 31/3203 is an IRIS MAZZA, born 4 December 1915, arriving Brisbane per ROMOLO on 26 December 1939. Neither is anybody here.

source: NAA — the Crupi internment dossiers, and a Civil Aliens Corps hypothesis tested and failed
scope: A direct test of a hypothesis published an hour earlier: that the Crupi brothers, released from internment in late 1943, would have Civil Aliens Corps files in NAA series J1737 as Rosario Mazza does.
result: THE HYPOTHESIS IS WRONG. The complete CRUPI name index — 233 items, all read — contains NO J1737 ITEM, NO «Civil Aliens Corps» and NO CAS service number for any Crupi. Rosario Mazza has one; neither of his wife's brothers does. Recorded as a negative rather than quietly dropped, because it was published as a plan and somebody would otherwise look for it again. WHAT IT MIGHT MEAN is unresolved: the Corps was not universal, and men released in October and December 1943 may simply have gone home to the cane. BUT THE SEARCH ANSWERED A BETTER QUESTION. ANTONINO CRUPI'S INTERNMENT DOSSIER IS NAA: MP1103/1, Q7838 — «Prisoner of War/Internee: Crupi, Antonio; Date of birth - 05 November 1907», Melbourne, 1942-1943, ACCESS OPEN; with its companion MP1103/2, Q7838. AND THE NUMBER CLOSES THE LOOP: his ALIENS REGISTRATION CARD, read this morning, carries «Q. 7838» beside his name. Same man, two series, one number. The identification no longer rests on birthplace alone. MARIO CRUPI LIKEWISE: MP1103/2, Q30124 — «Crupi, Mario; Year of birth - 1905». His aliens card gives «N.B.E. certificate Q30124». Same closure. A CONFLICT TO FLAG, NOT TO RESOLVE. The card gives Antonino's date of birth as «5.10.07» — 5 OCTOBER 1907 in Australian order. The dossier catalogue says «05 NOVEMBER 1907». One month apart, both from Commonwealth paperwork about the same man. The dossier itself would settle it; neither figure is preferred here. AND A THIRD ANTONIO CRUPI, WHO IS NOT OURS. MP1103/1 and MP1103/2, PWV11028: «Crupi, Antonio; Date of birth - 10 January 1904», a VICTORIAN internee — the PWV prefix against our Q. That is now the THIRD man of that name this archive has had to set aside, after the Serrata card at barcode 9209609 and the Silkwood East farmer on the 1959 roll. FINDING AID: NAA BP628/5, «Name Index and registration cards for internees dossiers Queensland - CACCIOLA to CURSIO», 1939-1962, Brisbane, OPEN. CRUPI falls inside that range, as MAZZA falls inside MACAUDO-MYSLIM.

source: NAA NameSearch — ARENA is 1650 items; ROCCO ARENA is nineteen, and one of them is ours
scope: NameSearch on ARENA across all record categories, then narrowed to the given name ROCCO.
result: ARENA IS NOT SWEEPABLE BY SURNAME: 1,650 ITEMS. It is a common Sicilian and Calabrian name and it is also a place -- «Arena» is a comune in the province of Vibo Valentia, and a D4028 card in the results belongs to a MICHELE VARTULI born at «Arena Catongaro». Writing out 1,650 rows would be a waste and reading them for surnames would invent relatives. THE DISCRIMINATOR HAS TO BE A GIVEN NAME. ROCCO ARENA IS NINETEEN ITEMS AND EXACTLY ONE IS THIS FAMILY: NAA: J25 1971/3900, «Arena, Rocco; wife Angelina [or Angela] [nee Polistena]», Brisbane, 1953-1971. THAT IS HIS ONLY RECORD IN THE WHOLE NAME INDEX -- no aliens card, no naturalisation, no arrival item of his own. He landed in December 1953, after the wartime series closed and before the Commonwealth started keeping much else on assisted Italians, and the one file that names him names him as a husband. THE OTHER EIGHTEEN, AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST IS AN INTERNMENT. A ROCCO ARENA WAS INTERNED IN AUSTRALIA: MP1103/1 and MP1103/2, PWN9406, «Date of birth - 31 AUGUST 1909»; an Aliens Tribunal objection, A367 C18000/298, «Objection No. 35»; C329 42, the same objection; C123 4326 and C123 ITALIAN INTERNEES [Box 611], both Sydney 1940; and ST1233/1 N35192, «Rocco Arena [Interned] [Application for Naturalisation]». HE IS NOT THIS FAMILY AND THE ARITHMETIC IS ABSOLUTE: this archive's Rocco Arena ARRIVED IN AUSTRALIA ON 27 DECEMBER 1953, thirteen years after that internment, and the Rocco Arena born at Scilla in 1861 DIED THERE ON 8 FEBRUARY 1932. Neither could have been in a Sydney camp in 1940. THIS ARCHIVE HAS JUST DOCUMENTED THREE INTERNED MEN IN THIS FAMILY, and a fourth of the right surname would be seized on. It is not one. THE REST, SO NOBODY RE-EXCLUDES THEM ONE BY ONE. A714 42/15084: Rocco Arena naturalised 25 June 1946, BORN GANZIRRI (Messina) 1907, resident Rose Bay NSW. SP11/5: arrived Sydney per REGINA D'ITALIA 3 October 1925. SP908/1 ITALIAN/ARENA ROCCO [1]: born 14 August 1942, arrived Sydney per ROMA 4 January 1963. SP908/1 [2]: born 6 September 1933, arrived Sydney per NEPTUNIA 3 October 1960. A435 1945/4/2718: born 3 February 1907. D4881: arrived Melbourne per GUGLIELMO MARCONI 2 March 1964, file at Adelaide. A1870 ARENA R: arrived Sydney per G MARCONI 13 May 1964. D400 SA1960/8987, D1915 SA17497, C3198 Z08102302J, B44 V1970/2215: South Australian, Sydney and Melbourne files without dates in their titles. SEVEN DISTINCT MEN AT LEAST, ON FIVE DIFFERENT BIRTH DATES, IN FIVE STATES. The surname plus the given name is still not an identification here; the arrival date is.

source: Antenati — Scilla, the birth Tavole of 1834, 1835 and 1836, P sections read complete
scope: CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA'S BIRTH. His son Giovanni's birth act of September 1883 makes him FORTY-EIGHT, so born about 1835, and his death act of 1924 names his parents GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO. Three years read across, not sampled -- 1834, 1835 and 1836 -- with the complete P section of each annual Tavola.
result: HE IS NOT IN ANY OF THEM, AND THE SHAPE OF THE ABSENCE IS THE FINDING. 1834 (container wR8Jg9p, 114 images, Tavola 107-114, 201 births): the P section is entries 140-164 and holds Paladino, Patafio, Piria, Parisi, Papalia, Boscaro, Pirrotta, Pizzarello, Poleo. NOT ONE POLISTENA. 1835 (container wbb2o4g, 136 images, Tavola 130-136, 206 births): P is entries 137-153 -- Paladino, Parenti, Prini, Pirrotta, Parisi, Panella, Priocca, Papalia, Patafio, Pugliese. NOT ONE POLISTENA. 1836 (container w6rZ7KQ, 126 images, Tavola 119-126, 222 births): P is entries 167-192 and holds EXACTLY ONE -- entry 191, «POLISTINA ANNUNZIATA, di GIUSEPPE e MARTELLO ANNA, 2 Dicembre». THREE YEARS, 629 BIRTHS, ONE POLISTENA. The P section at Scilla in the 1830s is Paladino and Pirrotta and Patafio; the Polistena are barely there. THIS BEARS ON THE WHOLE QUARTER: the Polistena may be incomers to Scilla rather than an old family of it, which would explain why this archive has never been able to push them above Camillo Antonio. AND THE ONE ENTRY IS A LEAD WITH A FLAW. «Giuseppe e Martello Anna» has the right two given names for Camillo Antonio's parents -- GIUSEPPE and ANNA -- and THE WRONG SURNAME for the mother: the death act of 1924 says ANNA PONTILLO. Either that index line is wrong, or the death act is, or these are two different couples. THE TAVOLA IS A FINDING AID AND THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN CAUGHT BY ONE BEFORE -- the 1854 index that called Serafina Arlotta «Rosa» and briefly turned a brother into a cousin. ACT 191 OF 1836 WOULD SETTLE IT and it is three images away. WORTH NOTING IN PASSING: 1836 entry 168 is «PONTILLO GIOVANNI, di Gius.e e Paladino Gius.a» -- a Pontillo household at Scilla with a Giuseppe at its head, in the same year and the same section. Pontillo and Polistena sitting four entries apart is exactly the circumstance in which a clerk writes one for the other. READ THE SAME HOUR, AND IT IS ACT 204, NOT 191 -- the Tavola's «Num. d'ordine» is an INDEX ROW and that index carries no act number at all; act 191 is a Squillaci birth at Solano. ACT 204: 2 DECEMBER 1836, the midwife TERESA ARENA declaring a girl born that morning to ANNA PONTILLO, 35, wife of GIUSEPPE POLISTINA, 38, MARINARO, named ANNUNZIATA. THE INDEX WAS WRONG AND THE DEATH ACT WAS RIGHT: the mother is PONTILLO, and ANNUNZIATA IS CAMILLO ANTONIO'S SISTER. It also dates Giuseppe Polistena to about 1798 and Anna Pontillo to about 1801, and gives the Polistena a trade -- MARINARO. NEXT: then widen to 1830-1833 and 1837-1840, since a declared age is a range and this archive has already been burned reading three points inside a window as a search of the window.

source: Antenati — Scilla births 1830–1840, ELEVEN consecutive P sections read for Camillo Antonio Polistena
scope: ELEVEN CONSECUTIVE YEARS, read across and not sampled: the complete P section of the annual birth Tavola for every year from 1830 to 1840. His son's 1883 birth act makes him forty-eight, so born about 1835, and his death act of 1924 names his parents GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO.
result: HE IS IN NONE OF THE ELEVEN, AND THE ELEVEN MAP THE WHOLE SURNAME AT SCILLA. Every Polistena birth in those years, with parents: 1830 -- POLISTINA ANTONINO, di LUIGI e MARIANNA BAVIERA, 23 Febbraio; POLISTINA SALVADORE, di FRANCESCO e GIUSEPPA LONGARDO, 9 Maggio. 1831 -- POLISTINA FRANCESCO ANTONIO, di LUIGI e GIOVANNA BAVIERA, 21 Giugno. 1832 -- POLISTINA DOMENICA, di FRANCESCO e GIUSEPPA LONGORDO, 17 Dicembre. 1833 -- POLISTINA ROCCO, DI GIUSEPPE E PONTILLO ANNA, 13 Dicembre. 1834, 1835 -- NONE. 1836 -- POLISTINA ANNUNZIATA, DI GIUSEPPE E ANNA PONTILLO, 2 Dicembre (atto 204, read in full; the Tavola misnames the mother MARTELLO). 1837, 1838 -- NONE. 1839 -- POLISTINA MARIA, di FRANCESCO e GIUSEPPA LONGARDO, 30 Maggio. 1840 -- POLISTINA FORTUNATA, DI GIUSEPPE E PONTILLO ANNA, 28 Gennaro. THREE HOUSEHOLDS, EIGHT BIRTHS, ELEVEN YEARS, ABOUT 2,100 CHILDREN. Giuseppe x Anna Pontillo (this archive's couple): Rocco 1833, Annunziata 1836, FORTUNATA 1840. Francesco x Giuseppa Longardo: Salvadore 1830, Domenica 1832, Maria 1839. Luigi x Marianna/Giovanna Baviera: Antonino 1830, Francesco Antonio 1831. AND THE SPACING IS THE ARGUMENT. This archive's couple have children in DECEMBER 1833, DECEMBER 1836 and JANUARY 1840 -- three years apart, twice over, with nothing before or between. 1830, 1831 and 1832 are read and hold no child of theirs, so ROCCO IS THE ELDEST and Camillo Antonio CANNOT be earlier. HE MUST BE 1841 OR LATER. THE NAMING CUSTOM AGREES. A first son takes the father's father's name, so Giuseppe's father was a ROCCO POLISTENA; a later son takes the mother's father's, which would make CAMILLO ANTONIO a namesake of a CAMILLO PONTILLO. Both point the search forward, not back. SO «FORTY-EIGHT» IN SEPTEMBER 1883 IS WRONG BY AT LEAST SIX YEARS. Anna Pontillo was about thirty-five in 1836, so she could bear children to about 1846. THE WINDOW IS NOW 1841-1848, and no container for any of those years has been bought. ONE FREE CORROBORATION IN PASSING: the 1830 A section, entry 2, reads «ARLOTTA SERAFINA -- GIOVANNI, e COSTA MARIA -- 13 Giugno». source: Antenati — Scilla, Nati 1833 atto 174, read in the original
scope: Rocco Polistina's birth act, to confirm the 1833 Tavola line and get his parents' ages from a second independent document. Found by date, since that index carries no act number: three probes bracketing 13 December.
result: READ, AND IT DOES THREE THINGS. ONE, IT CONFIRMS THE PARENTS FROM A SECOND ACT. GIUSEPPE POLISTINA, THIRTY-FOUR, MARINARO, and ANNA PONTILLO, THIRTY-THREE, in December 1833; against thirty-eight and thirty-five in December 1836. Three years of register, four and two of declared age -- the ordinary slop of this register, and both acts land on Giuseppe born 1798-99 and Anna born 1800-01. No conflict. TWO, THE SAME MIDWIFE DELIVERED BOTH CHILDREN. TERESA ARENA, thirty-eight here and forty-four in 1836, LEVATRICE, declared both births in person and produced the witnesses at both. THREE, AND IT IS THE ONE WORTH CARRYING: THE MARGIN CARRIES A MARRIAGE ADDED THIRTY-SIX YEARS LATER. «L'anno 1869, il giorno 12 Luglio -- il sottoscritto Uffiziale dello Stato Civile dichiara che ROCCO POLISTINA, cui ha rapporto il contro scritto atto di nascita, HA CONTRATTO MATRIMONIO IN QUESTO COMUNE CON COLORINA BRI[...] nel giorno 12 andante mese ed anno. L'Uffiziale G. Zagari. Reggio 26 Agosto 1869.» So he lived to thirty-five and married at Scilla on 12 JULY 1869. The bride's surname is cut by the binding and her forename reads COLORINA or COLOMBA; recorded as read and flagged, because the 1869 marriage act will give it plainly and this archive has been burned by a name guessed off an index before. THE METHOD POINT: SCILLA'S RESTAURAZIONE BIRTH ACTS CARRY MARGINAL ANNOTATIONS ADDED DECADES LATER, and this archive has never looked at one. A birth act is not only a birth. Camillo Antonio Polistena's own act, when it is found, may carry his marriage in the same hand -- and so may the Arena and Arlotta birth acts already read, whose margins nobody has examined.

source: Antenati — three Scilla birth-act MARGINS read, and the annotation rule calibrated
scope: Row 154, opened an hour earlier: Scilla birth acts carry marginal annotations added decades later, and this archive had never looked at one. Three margins tested -- Rocco Polistina 1833, Serafina Arlotta 1830, Filippo Arena 1852 -- on containers already bought.
result: ONE ANNOTATED, TWO BLANK, AND THE RULE IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKED. ROCCO POLISTINA, Nati 1833 atto 174: margin carries his marriage AT SCILLA on 12 JULY 1869, signed and dated from Reggio six weeks later. SERAFINA ARLOTTA, Nati 1830 atto 89: MARGIN EMPTY. She married at Scilla on 7 February 1851. FILIPPO ARENA, Nati 1852 atto 48: MARGIN EMPTY. Any marriage of his would fall after 1866. THE READING THAT FITS ALL THREE: the annotation is an ITALIAN-ERA habit, absent from an 1851 marriage and present on an 1869 one, AND it is written only when the later act is registered in the SAME COMUNE -- the note says «ha contratto matrimonio IN QUESTO COMUNE» in so many words. SO A BLANK MARGIN IS WEAK EVIDENCE. For a pre-1866 marriage it means nothing whatever. For a post-1866 one it is consistent with a marriage somewhere else -- which for Filippo Arena is the reading the rest of the evidence already supports. TWO ACTS READ IN THE REGISTER FOR THE FIRST TIME AS A BY-PRODUCT. NATI 1830 ATTO 89 confirms that the certified copy bound into the 1851 processetti is FAITHFUL word for word -- worth knowing, since a Pizzo extract once lost ten years off a man's age. NATI 1852 ATTO 48, Filippo Arena's birth, carried here until today off the Tavola alone: 14 FEBRUARY 1852, before GAETANO FERRANTE, sindaco; ANTONIO ARENA, di anni TRENTASEI, MARINARO, and SERAFINA ARLOTTA, di anni VENTOTTO; witnesses ROCCO PIZZARELLO, 30, FERRARO, and TOMMASO CARDONA, 30, FALEGNAME; THE DECLARANT COULD NOT WRITE. AND ITS AGES ARE THE WORST THIS ARCHIVE HAS SEEN IN ONE LINE: he was thirty-two and she was twenty-one. FOUR YEARS AND SEVEN YEARS OUT. Two years later the same couple are entered as thirty-four and twenty-two, which fits. The clerk guessed. This is now the act to point at whenever a declared age is about to identify somebody.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Nati 1853 atto 53 and the margins of 1852-1853, read in the original
scope: Row 154: check the margins of Scilla birth acts already fetched. Started with «Domenico Arena, Nati 1853 atto 2», one of the three brothers who vanish after 1898.
result: THE MARGIN WAS THE SMALL FIND. THE ACT WAS THE BIG ONE. ACT 2 OF 1853 IS NOT HIM. It is DOMENICA BELLANTONI, born 4 January to Maria Bellantoni, filatrice, twenty-nine, who acknowledged her as her natural daughter. «2» was a TAVOLA ROW NUMBER -- the second entry in the A block -- exactly as Serafina Arlotta's «atto 2» of 1830 turned out to be act 89 earlier today. Both are «atto 2» because a surname-ordered A block puts Arena and Arlotta second. THE REAL ACT IS 53, FOUND BY DATE IN FOUR PROBES -- and it says the child is a GIRL. «FRANCESCANTONIO ARENA, DI ANNI TRENTADUE, MARINARO ... ci à presentato UNA FEMINA ... nata da SERAFINA ARLOTTA, sua moglie legittima, DI ANNI VENTIDUE ... di dare alla FANCIULLA il nome di DOMENICA», and the Indicazione column records the baptism of DOMENICA ARENA. THREE STATEMENTS IN ONE ACT. SO ROCCO ARENA'S «BROTHER DOMENICO» IS HIS SISTER DOMENICA, and this archive carried her as a son for fourteen weeks without opening the act. AND THE AGES IN THIS ACT ARE EXACT -- thirty-two and twenty-two, both landing on the known birth dates -- fourteen months after the 1852 act made the same couple thirty-six and twenty-eight. Individual acts are right or wrong; the register is not drifting. THE MARGINS, WITH A CONTROL THIS TIME. 1852 act 55: «Atto 18 Febbraio 1881 N. 11 -- SCARFONE ROCCO contrasse matrimonio in Scilla con VITA MARIA». 1853 act 54: a marriage of 20 December 1876. 1853 act 55: «PALADINO SANTA contrasse matrimonio in Scilla», 8 September 1883. SO THE PRACTICE IS LIVE IN BOTH VOLUMES -- and FILIPPO ARENA'S MARGIN (1852 act 48) IS EMPTY. That upgrades an hour-old grading: a blank margin here is evidence, not nothing. HE DID NOT MARRY AT SCILLA. ONE CORRECTION OF MY OWN, MADE AND THEN UNMADE WITHIN THE HOUR: I first took writing at the right edge of the 1852 act-48 opening for act 49's margin. It is act 49's BAPTISM column. The control had to be run properly on a different opening before the blank meant anything.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Nati 1860 atto 45, and the annotation inference disproved
scope: Row 154 continued: Giuseppe Arena's birth act, one of the two brothers who vanish after 1898, and a man KNOWN to have married at Scilla on 12 September 1885. A control case for the annotation rule, chosen because the answer was already known.
result: THE CONTROL FAILS THE RULE, AND THE RULE IS WITHDRAWN. Act 45 of 1860 is Giuseppe Arena's birth -- the Tavola number is the act number here, unlike 1830 and 1853 -- declared 6 MARCH 1860 by the midwife GIUSEPPA DE GIROLAMO, twenty-three, for a boy born the fifth at ten o'clock to SERAFINA ARLOTTA, twenty-nine, and FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA, marinaro. The date matches this archive exactly and Serafina's age is exact. AND THE ANNOTATION BOX IS EMPTY. GIUSEPPE ARENA MARRIED MARIA MARTELLO AT SCILLA ON 12 SEPTEMBER 1885 -- act 73, read here in the original -- and nothing was ever written back into his birth act. So a blank box does NOT mean a man did not marry in the comune, and the inference drawn against FILIPPO ARENA an hour earlier is withdrawn in full. Filippo's blank margin now means nothing at all. WHAT SURVIVES OF ROW 154: a PRESENT annotation is still free evidence -- Rocco Polistina's marriage of 12 July 1869 came that way, and marriages of 1876, 1881 and 1883 sit on other acts. IT IS A BONUS WHEN IT IS THERE AND SILENCE WHEN IT IS NOT. AND THE BOX MOVES BETWEEN VOLUMES. 1852 and 1853 use a LEFT column headed «MARGINE per scriversi alcune notizie riguardanti gli atti di Nascita». 1860 uses a RIGHT box headed «MENZIONI prescritte dagli articoli 64, 65 e 106, LL. CC.». Same purpose, opposite side of the page. Anybody reporting «the margin is blank» must say which side they looked at. ONE MORE CAUTION SOFTENED: this archive records that when a LEVATRICE declares, the act gives the parents WITHOUT ages. Here a levatrice declared and both ages are given. A tendency, not a rule.

source: Antenati — Scilla births 1843, 1844 and 1845, completing the window round Camillo Antonio Polistena
scope: Three more P sections after the eleven-year sweep of 1830-1840 and the 1841-1842 pass. With these, the Scilla birth index has been read for SIXTEEN CONSECUTIVE YEARS, 1830 to 1845.
result: HE IS IN NONE OF THEM, AND HIS PARENTS' CHILDBEARING AT SCILLA IS NOW BOUNDED. 1843 (container LD6b47G -- the SECOND ark of a doubled year; an_ua2002874 holds the acts and closes at act 200 with no index, an_ua2002877 carries the Tavola at images 16-21, badly soiled): the P block holds Pizzarello, Papalia, Paladino, Princi, Patafio, Pirrotta, Perina, Piccone, Porchi, Pontillo, Poleo. NO POLISTINA AS A CHILD. One as a MOTHER, for the third time: «Pirrotta Antonia -- Rocco e POLISTINA ANNUNZIATA». 1844 (container LNolOVK, 111 images, Tavola 104-111, 192 births): TWO Polistina, entries 131 and 133 -- «POLISTINA ROCCO, di DOM.co e COSTA CAROLINA» and «POLISTINA GIUSEPPE, di FRAN.co e LONGORDO GIUSEPPA». Both are the OTHER households. Neither is Giuseppe x Anna Pontillo. 1845 (container 5gGp2Rz, 120 images, Tavola 114-120, 210 births): PARTIAL. The P block runs entries 145-170 and SEVEN OF THE EIGHTEEN LINES ARE TOO FAINT TO READ -- 145, 147, 150, 151, 153, 154 and 157. No Polistina among the legible ones, but that is NOT a clean negative and is not recorded as one. The volume needs a second look at higher contrast. SO THE SHAPE OF THE FAMILY IS NOW FIXED. GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO have children at Scilla in DECEMBER 1833, DECEMBER 1836 and JANUARY 1840 -- and in the twelve other years read, NOTHING. Anna was about thirty-five in 1836, so her childbearing plausibly ends around 1840-42, which is exactly what the register shows. AND THAT LEAVES A CONTRADICTION THIS ARCHIVE SHOULD STATE RATHER THAN SMOOTH. Camillo Antonio Polistena's death act of 1924 names these two as his parents. His son's birth act of 1883 makes him forty-eight. THERE IS NO YEAR IN THEIR CHILDBEARING WINDOW WHERE HE FITS, AND THE WINDOW HAS BEEN READ ACROSS. Four readings, none preferred here: (1) he was born somewhere else and the family came to Scilla; (2) the 1924 death act's parents are wrong; (3) the Tavola omitted him -- these indexes DO drop entries, and 1898's death index carries an Arena with no act number at all; (4) he is one of the children already found under a name this archive has not connected. THE TEST THAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM is his MARRIAGE act to Giovanna Romano, about 1870-1880, which would give his age a third time and his birthplace outright. Scilla's Italian-era marriages 1866-1913 are all on Antenati and the series is already listed in scilla-arks-italiano.tsv.

SO FOUR YEARS ARE DONE: 1874, 1876 and 1877 read and CLEAR; 1875 has no index and must be read act by act. THE INDEX FORMAT IS THE SAME GOOD ONE IN ALL THREE -- every spouse alphabetical, the two halves of each couple BRACED against one register number -- so a year costs ONE crop once the container is in hand. LEFT: 1870, 1871, 1872, 1873 (containers not bought), 1875 (by acts), 1878-1882 (not bought). 1879 AND 1880 ADDED, BOTH CLEAR, AND THE SWEEP IS NOW FIVE YEARS DEEP. 1879 (container LzmZQnm, 38 images, Indice Annuale at 37-38): P is PROCOPIO Giuseppe x Galte Giovanna (38), PAPALIA Antonio x Papalia Anna Maria (2), PAPALIA Pasquale x Ciccone Carmena (5), PALADINI Davide x Paladino Mariantonia (46), PAPALIA Domenico x Papalia Angela (52), PALADINO Vittoria x Melidoni Gaetano (49) and PRIGANDE Bruno x Legato Domenica (3). NO POLISTENA. 1880 (container w6zPDGm, 31 images, Indice at 30-31): P is PASPIGLIA Giorgio x Lagana Pasqualina (8), PIRIA Giuseppe x Macri Angela (20), PIRROTTA Francesco x Bova Giuseppa (22), PALADINO Francesco Rocco x Giordano Grazia (28), PATAFIO Antonino x Patafio Maria (30), PAPALIA Pasquale x Bueti Angela (34) and PAPALIA Antonino x Papalia Petrucia (44). THREE THINGS NOTED AND DELIBERATELY NOT JOINED. 1879 act 22: ARLOTTA GIUSEPPE marries -- the first entry in that year's index. Serafina Arlotta's brother GIUSEPPE ANTONIO ARLOTTA is recorded here as the husband of Angela Nunziata Pizzarello, and the bride's name in this index is not obviously hers, so the act is wanted before anything is claimed. 1879 act 8: RUSSO GIOVANNI x ARENA FORTUNATA -- the Russo-Arena pairing again, six years before Giovanni Arena married Concetta Russo. 1880 act 40: RIGANATI ANTONIO x ARENA TERESA -- and the Teresa Arena this archive holds, Orazio's daughter born 1853, died in 1913 as the wife of PIETRO BOVA. Either a different woman or a first marriage; nothing here decides it. SO: 1874, 1876, 1877, 1879 and 1880 READ AND CLEAR. 1875 has no index. 1878 not bought. Left: 1870-1873, 1878, 1881, 1882. 1878 AND 1882 ADDED, AND 1882 IS THE FIRST YEAR THE SURNAME APPEARS AT ALL. 1878 (container 5Yb6Q2v, 29 images, Indice at 27-29, badly water-stained but legible): P is PALADINO Cesare x Bova Antonia (7), PORPIGLIA Giuseppe x Pirrotta Rosaria (13), PALERMO Paolo x Pirrotta Annunziata (29), PIZZARELLO Giuseppe x Ida Maria (35), and Martello Domenico x PATAFIO Serafina (38). THAT IS WORTH MORE THAN A NEGATIVE. Seven years of this index have now been read and 1882 is the FIRST to hold the surname at all -- so the Polistena were marrying at Scilla by 1882, and the earlier silence is not an artefact of the index. AND «LUIGI CARMELO» IS A NAME THIS ARCHIVE HAS MET: the 1831 birth Tavola gives «Polistina Francesco Antonio, di LUIGI e Giovanna Baviera», the third of the four Scilla Polistena households. A Luigi Carmelo marrying in 1882 fits that line as a son or grandson and fits nothing here. SO: 1874, 1876, 1877, 1878, 1879, 1880 and 1882 READ. 1875 has no index. 1881's container lookup returned 403 twice and is not bought. Left: 1870-1873, 1881, and 1875 by acts. THE TWO 1882 ACTS ARE WORTH OPENING ANYWAY -- a Scilla marriage act of that date gives both spouses' ages, BOTH BIRTHPLACES and all four parents, so either one would say whether the Polistena of Scilla were born there or came in, which is the question row 137 could not answer from sixteen years of births. NAVIGATION NOTE FOR THE 1882 VOLUME, BOUGHT WITH FOUR WASTED PROBES. Container wErAXdW, 40 images. IT IS SPLIT INTO TWO SERIES AND BOTH ARE NUMBERED FROM ONE. Image 33 carries a margin reading «Numero 4 -- Colosi Giuseppe Luigi Vincenzo / Zagari Giuseppa Maria Raffaela», which is PARTE II act 4, not parte I act 4 -- parte II begins around image 31 and is the register of marriages celebrated elsewhere and transcribed here. source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1881 atto 4: Camillo Antonio Polistena x Giovanna Romano, FOUND
scope: Row 155, closed. Eight years of the Scilla marriage index read; 1881's Indice Annuale gave the entry and the margin-strip montage gave the image in two calls.
result: FOUND. SCILLA, MATRIMONI 1881, ATTO 4 -- 23 JANUARY 1881 at six seventeen in the evening. POLISTINA CAMILLO ANTONIO, DI ANNI TRENTASEI, MARINARO, NATO IN QUESTO COMUNE, figlio del FU GIUSEPPE e della FU ANNA PONTILLO. ROMANO GIOVANNA, DI ANNI VENTISEI, FILATRICE, NATA IN QUESTO COMUNE, figlia di ANNUNZIATO e di ANGELA ZIRILLI, both living. THE AGE IS THE FINDING. THIRTY-SIX in January 1881 is a birth about 1844 -- and his son's birth act of September 1883 makes him FORTY-EIGHT, a birth about 1835. NINE YEARS APART. The 1835 figure is what this archive swept eleven years of birth Tavole around, and the answer was never in them. THE MARRIAGE ACT IS PREFERRED, on the rule this archive has already applied to Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa: a man appearing in person to marry, with the parish papers checked, against a father registering a newborn in the evening. HE WAS BORN AT SCILLA -- «nato in questo Comune» -- so the birth act EXISTS and the sixteen-year sweep missed it. AND 1844 IS INSIDE THAT SWEEP: the 1844 P block was read for entries 127-138 WITHOUT ESTABLISHING WHERE THE BLOCK ENDS, and 1845 is on record as PARTIAL with seven of eighteen lines too faint. Those two years are now the shortest road left, and they are years already paid for. THREE MORE THINGS THE ACT GIVES. GIUSEPPE POLISTENA AND ANNA PONTILLO WERE BOTH DEAD BY JANUARY 1881 -- the first bound either has had, against their last sighting alive in January 1840. The parentage is confirmed from a SECOND document, forty-three years before the 1924 death act. And GIOVANNA ROMANO is dated -- twenty-six, born at Scilla about 1854 -- with ANNUNZIATO ROMANO and ANGELA ZIRILLI both alive, which is the FOURTH record to call her a Romano and the first in which she is the subject. METHOD: the margin-strip montage found the act in two calls. Images 2-7 carry acts 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 in the left margin with BOTH SPOUSES' NAMES, so act 4 is the right-hand act of image 3. The same trick that had been written down, ignored, and then vindicated on the 1882 volume an hour earlier.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Nati 1844 Tavola entry 142: Camillo Antonio Polistena's birth, FOUND
scope: Row 137, closed. His marriage act of January 1881 made him thirty-six, pointing at 1844 -- a year already read and recorded as clear. It was not clear; the reading was.
result: HE IS AT ENTRY 142 OF THE 1844 TAVOLA: «POLISTINA CAMILLO -- GIUSEPPE e PONTILLO ANNA -- 21 SETTEMBRE». BORN AT SCILLA ON 21 SEPTEMBER 1844. THE ARITHMETIC IS EXACT, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT SAFE. He was THIRTY-SIX YEARS AND FOUR MONTHS at his marriage on 23 January 1881, and the act says «trentasei». He was THIRTY-EIGHT AND ELEVEN MONTHS at his son's birth on 16 September 1883, and that act says FORTY-EIGHT -- ten years wrong, and the figure this archive searched around for sixteen years. AND THE REASON IT TOOK SO LONG IS MINE. The 1844 P block was read EARLIER THE SAME DAY. The crop covered entries 127 to 138 and stopped; the row was written saying that the end of the block had not been established, and then 1845, 1830-1832 and five marriage years were swept instead of spending one more crop on the year already open. HE IS FOUR ENTRIES PAST WHERE I STOPPED. THE RULE THIS BUYS, AND IT IS THE SECOND OF ITS KIND HERE: A PARTIAL READING RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE IS THE SAME ERROR AS A 403 RECORDED AS A NIL. This archive already controls for the second. Where a section is read, FIND ITS END -- the next section letter -- before writing «not there». 1845 is still on record as PARTIAL with seven faint lines and should be finished on the same principle. A FIFTH POLISTENA HOUSEHOLD CAME WITH IT: entry 143, the very next line, is «POLISTINA TOMMASO -- D. ANTONIO e PALADINO ANNUNZIATA», the «D.» being DON. NEXT, AND CHEAP: the ACT. The Tavola carries no act number and the register runs in date order, so 21 September 1844 is two or three probes into container LNolOVK. The act would give BOTH PARENTS' AGES -- dating Giuseppe Polistena and Anna Pontillo a third time -- and may carry a marriage annotation in its margin. THE ACT ITSELF WAS HUNTED THE SAME HOUR AND NOT FOUND -- FIVE ACTS ELIMINATED, WRITTEN DOWN SO NOBODY CHECKS THEM AGAIN. The 1844 volume maps cleanly: image N carries folio N-2, with the EVEN act on the left page and the ODD act on the right. Image 73 = folio 71 = acts 140 and 141; image 74 = folio 72 = acts 142 and 143. CHECKED AND EXCLUDED, all in the September run: ACT 138 (declarant Domenico Spoletti, child Alberto...), ACT 139 (child Giuseppe), ACT 140 (declarant Cosmo Bellantoni, child MARIANNA VIOLANTE), ACT 141 (declarant Domenico Calarco, baptised at the parish OF SOLANO), ACT 142 (declarant Giovanni Macri, mother a Barbaro of thirty, child ROSANTONIO, born the 28th). NONE IS POLISTINA. SO EITHER THE ACT SITS OUTSIDE 138-142 -- the September acts plausibly run 135 to 145 -- or the Tavola's «21 Settembre» is the BIRTH date against a later declaration, or that faint line reads a different day. THE FINDING DOES NOT DEPEND ON IT: the Tavola gives the parents and the date, and the marriage act's «trentasei» is exact for 21 September 1844 to the month. But THE ACT HAS NOT BEEN READ, and this archive's own rule says the index is not the source. NEXT PASS: montage the act-number-and-date band (region pct:50,10,48,20 at width 900 works) across images 68-76, which covers acts 132 to 149 in one look, instead of opening them one at a time as I did. AND THEN IT WAS FOUND, WITH THE TWO MONTAGES THAT SHOULD HAVE COME FIRST. One montage of the EVEN acts across images 68-77 mapped the year: September runs acts 129-143, October begins at 144. One montage of the ODD acts across images 68-73 put a POLISTINA at ACT 137. ATTO 137 OF 1844: «e comparso GIUSEPPE POLISTINA, DI ANNI CINQUANTA, MARINARO ... quale ci a presentato un MASCHIO ... nato da ANNA PONTILLO, FILATRICE, sua moglie legittima ... NEL GIORNO VENTUNO CORRENTE MESE ... di dare al fanciullo IL NOME DI CAMILLO ANTONIO.» The Indicazione column names the baptism of CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTINA. SO THE TAVOLA WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE DATE AND THE PARENTS AND WRONG ABOUT THE NUMBER -- 142 was its row, 137 is the act -- WHICH IS THE THIRD TIME TODAY. And the act adds the full given name, CAMILLO ANTONIO, where the index gives only «Camillo». AND THE MARGIN CARRIES HIS MARRIAGE, annotated «Scilla 25 Gennaio 1881» -- two days after the wedding of 23 January 1881. The birth act and the marriage act point at each other across thirty-seven years. FIVE ACTS WERE OPENED ONE AT A TIME BEFORE THE MONTAGES WERE USED. That is the whole lesson: the montage is not a last resort, it is the first move in any volume whose index does not give act numbers.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1815 atto 29: Filippo Arena x Domenica Costa, FOUND

source: Antenati — the act-head montage, proved on three unindexed marriage volumes
scope: Method. A restauration and napoleonic marriage opening puts the END of one act on the left page and the HEAD of the next on the right: «Num. d'Ordine», the date, the groom's name, his age, his trade and his father. Cropping pct:52,18,46,26 at width 900 and tiling ten to a sheet reads a whole volume in four or five images.
result: IT WORKS, AND IT REPLACES THE ANNUAL TAVOLA. 111 acts across 1815, 1816 and 1817 read in fourteen montages and three single crops. source: Antenati — twenty-one Scilla marriage containers, 1820-1843, banked in one sitting

source: Antenati — Scilla processetti 1815, bundle 29: the Arena-Costa marriage file, READ ENTIRE
scope: Row 159. Container LqA4a7D, 364 images covering 1815 and 1816. Found by scanning wrappers -- they carry the year, the folio range, the bundle number and the couple in three words -- at five-image spacing, then two at step two to close in.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo relisted in full: 457 registers, not the 103 this archive held
scope: The whole holding in one page load, `?localita=Piedimonte Etneo&s_size=500`, parsed in page context and verified group by group against the live listing -- every fondo, type, ark range, count and year list reconciled before anything was written.
result: THE ARCHIVE HELD LESS THAN A QUARTER OF IT. 457 registers: 223 restaurazione, 225 italiano, and NINE «RIVELI DI ANIME E DI TERRE» of the Deputazione del Regno, 1714 and 1747-1752, which nobody here knew existed. What had never been listed at all: every italiano year after 1863, all the ALLEGATI and PUBBLICAZIONI, the Diversi, the Cittadinanze, and the twenty volumes of MATRIMONI PROCESSETTI 1841-1860. THE HOLDING STOPS AT 1893 -- so Venera Cassaneti's death in 1925 and the Mazza-Nicotra marriage of about 1900 are NOT on Antenati and never were.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1875 searched for Maria Nicotra
scope: Her tree year. The annual index (images 99-101, alphabetical by surname) holds exactly one «Nicotra Maria», act 34, and the act was read in the original.
result: READ, AND ELIMINATED ON THE MARGIN. Act 34 is Maria Nicotra born 6 March 1875 in via San Basile to ALFIO NICOTRA, sixty-eight, bracciante, and ANGELA PREVITERA -- not John Nicotra and Venera Cassaneti. Her marginal annotation settles it: «Unita in matrimonio con Nicito Giuseppe fu Vincenzo con atto del 29.7.91 iscritto in Piedimonte Etneo». Ours married SALVATORE MAZZA and died at Brisbane in 1963. 1875 IS CLOSED, and the method for the rest is now fixed: read each year's index for Nicotra Maria, then read that act's MARGIN, which names the husband and identifies ours in one crop.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1879 index read whole: no Salvatore Mazza, and no Nicotra at all
scope: Row 161 and the Salvatore Mazza birth year. The Indice Annuale at images 78-80, alphabetical by surname; M and N sections read at native width.
result: TWO NEGATIVES FOR ONE INDEX READ. The M section of 1879 holds «Mazza Rosaria 167» and «Mazza Venerio 205» and NO Salvatore -- so the tree's «Salvatore Mazza 1879» has no birth act at Piedimonte in that year, and this archive's link to NATI 1873 ATTO 3 stands with a negative behind it instead of only a reading. The N section holds Neri, Nicodemo and Nucifora and NO NICOTRA WHATEVER, so 1879 is closed for Maria Nicotra too. The index also caught «Mazza Rosaria 167», a possible sister of Salvatore, not yet opened. AND THE REACH IS NOW KNOWN, AND IT WAS NEVER HER TOWN. This sweep could reach exactly one thing: children registered AT PIEDIMONTE ETNEO. Maria Nicotra was registered at MASCALI, the next comune -- Nati 1875 atto 144, read 21 September -- because her father Giovanni Nicotra was «domiciliato e residente a Mascali» and a wife went to her husband's comune. So the Nicotra nil in this year is TRUE AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT HER. What it does still say, and this part stands, is that no SALVATORE MAZZA was registered at Piedimonte in 1879.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1873 atto 3: read in full, and its margin is EMPTY
scope: Row 161. The act was already cited here from an earlier reading; what had never been looked at was its MARGINAL ANNOTATION, which in this series names the subject's spouse and the date and comune of the marriage -- the instrument that identified and eliminated the 1875 Maria Nicotra in one crop.
result: THE ACT IS RICHER THAN THE CITATION AND THE MARGIN IS BLANK. «Rosario Mazza DI MARIANO, di anni ventotto, bracciante» presented a son born 5 January 1873 at seven in the morning to his wife «LEONARDA BONANNO DI GAETANO», in CONTRADA TERREMORTE, named SALVADORE. The patronymics confirm Mariano Mazza and Gaetano Bonanno from a second act. But the annotation column beside it is EMPTY, where the act four lines down carries a full marriage annotation -- so this route does not locate Salvatore's marriage to Maria Nicotra, and a blank box proves nothing either way. ALSO WORTH RECORDING: the opening is photographed TWICE, once with an archivist's masking card over the right page and once with it moved. The card covered this act entirely on image 3; image 4 shows it whole.

source: The archive's own chart — /tree/ now draws people the family tree does not contain
scope: Rows 51 and 63. The blocker was recorded as «the charts are the shared kit's and this archive leaves the kit alone». Re-read the kit instead of working around it.
result: THE KIT HAD ALREADY LEFT THE DOOR OPEN AND SAID SO IN A COMMENT. `lineage()` takes `parentsOf(row)` from the caller, and `kit/lib/ahnen.js` reads: «returning a row that is not in the file is allowed and is the point: a parent known only as a name on a register is still a real thing the chart should draw, and refusing it would quietly shorten the line.» So `/tree/`'s own parentsOf now falls back to `documented-parents.json` where the export gives a person no parents -- NOT where it gives them parents, because the chart is a drawing of the tree and silently redrawing it would be lying about the source. ROSARIO MAZZA'S LINE NO LONGER ENDS AT A CARD SAYING «Before Piedimonte Etneo, 1850»: MARIANO MAZZA and MARIA CATALANO now stand above him, graded as documented, unlinked because they have no person page. Nothing in the kit was touched and no fork was made.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo birth indexes swept for a Maria Nicotra: 1870, 1871, 1873, 1874, 1876
scope: Row 161. Each year's Indice Annuale read in the original at the N section, every entry named. With 1875 and 1879, read separately, that is SEVEN years.
result: NOT ONE MARIA NICOTRA IN ANY OF THEM, and the N sections are short enough to quote whole. 1870: Nicodemo Antonino di Giuseppe 74, NICOTRA FILIPPA di Leonardo 76, Nucifora Leonarda di Salvatore 179. 1871: NICOTRA SALVATORE 17, NICOTRA GIOVANNI 52. 1873: Nicodemo Francesco 87, NICOTRA IGNAZIO 86. 1874: Nicodemo Francesco 177, Nucifora Salvatore 185. 1876: Nicolosi Francesco 89, Nucifora Giovanni 156, Nucifora Alfio 181, Nicodemo Rosario 180. The Nicotra are at Piedimonte -- five births in five years -- but they are not producing a Maria. USEFUL BY-PRODUCT: the indexes of 1870 and 1872 are written «Surname Given DI FATHER», so the patronymic is in the index itself and a candidate can be confirmed or dismissed without opening the act.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1872: no Maria Nicotra, and a Mazza child the tree lacks
scope: Row 161. The Indice Annuale at images 77-78, two openings, read whole at the M and N sections.
result: THE N SECTION IS NICOTRA ANGELO 147, NICOTRA GIOVANNA 158, NUCIFORA FRANCESCA 162 -- no Maria, which closes an eighth year. THE M SECTION PAID INSTEAD: «MAZZA MARIANO -- 32». Act 32 read in the original: born 12 February 1872 in CONTRADA SAN BASILIO to «ROSARIO MAZZA DI MARIANO, d'anni ventisette, bracciante» and «LEONARDA BONANNO DI GAETANO». Salvatore Mazza's elder brother, the naming custom pointing straight back at Mariano Mazza (b. c. 1809), and Rosario's age confirming 1845 for the third time. The Mazza and the Nicotra were neighbours at Piedimonte, which argues for reading the rest of the Piedimonte years before reaching for Catania.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1877: no Nicotra at all, and a second Rosario Mazza
scope: Row 161. The Indice Annuale at images 102-105, M and N sections read at native width; then two Mazza acts opened off the M section.

The M section held «Mazza Antonino 164» and «Mazza Orazio 168», and act 168 is the find: a Rosario Mazza, thirty-one, whose wife is ALSO called Leonarda -- LEONARDA MONACORSO, contadina, in VIA GROTTA NICODEMO. A SECOND ROSARIO-AND-LEONARDA AT PIEDIMONTE. Ours is «Rosario Mazza DI MARIANO» with Leonarda Bonanno in contrada San Basilio; the patronymic and the street are what tell them apart, and the family tree's own Orazio Mazza, born 1883 to a Rosario and a Leonarda, is precisely who this act would have been hung on. ALSO BANKED: an act-to-image map for this volume -- each opening carries two acts on the left page and one or two on the right, and the openings are photographed TWICE, once with the archivist's card over the left page.

source: Antenati — the WHOLE DECADE 1870-1879 of Piedimonte births read for Maria Nicotra
scope: Row 161. Ten consecutive annual indexes, every N section read in the original at native width and every entry named. Not a sample: the decade.
result: TEN YEARS, TEN N SECTIONS, AND NOT ONE MARIA NICOTRA WHO COULD BE HERS. 1870 Nicotra Filippa; 1871 Nicotra Salvatore, Nicotra Giovanni; 1872 Nicotra Angelo, Nicotra Giovanna; 1873 Nicotra Ignazio; 1874 none; 1875 ONE Maria Nicotra, eliminated on her own margin, which marries her to Giuseppe Nicito at Piedimonte in 1891; 1876 none; 1877 none; 1878 Nicotra Alfio twice; 1879 none. THE SURNAME IS THERE THROUGHOUT and the family is having children; it is simply not having this one. A DECADE IS NOT A SAMPLE, and the year she should be in is the year she is most clearly absent from. The tree's «born 1875 at Piedimonte Etneo» now has a complete decade against its comune. What it does NOT yet have against it is 1866-1869 and 1880-1884, and those get read before anything is concluded.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1880 and 1881 read for Maria Nicotra
scope: Row 161. Both annual indexes read at the N section in the original; 1881's N block is split across two openings and both halves were read, because a section that ends at the foot of a page is exactly where a partial reading turns into a false negative.
result: TWELVE CONSECUTIVE YEARS NOW, 1870-1881, AND STILL NO MARIA NICOTRA. 1880's N section is a single entry, NUCIFORA FRANCESCO 92 -- no Nicotra at all. 1881's is NICOTRA ANTONINA 24 at the foot of one opening, continuing on the next with NUCIFORA CONCETTA, NUCIFORA AGATA, NICOTRA MARIANO and NERI CONCETTA. A LEAD NOT YET OPENED: the 1880 M section carries «MAZZA GAETANO -- 66», and GAETANO is the name the Sicilian custom gives a SECOND son -- the mother's father. Leonarda Bonanno's father is Gaetano Bonanno. That act may be another child of Rosario and Leonarda, or another of the town's Mazza households; it has not been opened and nothing is claimed. AND THE REACH IS NOW KNOWN, AND IT WAS NEVER HER TOWN. These indexes cover births registered AT PIEDIMONTE ETNEO and nothing else. Maria Nicotra was born at MASCALI on 8 December 1875 (Nati 1875 atto 144) to Giovanni Nicotra, a Mascali man, and Venera Cassaniti. Fourteen consecutive Piedimonte indexes were read carefully and could never have held her. THE NIL IS A FACT ABOUT THE COMUNE THAT WAS SEARCHED, not about the family.

source: NAA NameSearch — MAZZA Maria and NICOTRA, all records
scope: Row 161, asking the other side of the question. Twelve years of Piedimonte birth indexes have not produced her; her own Australian papers would give her birthplace directly, without another Italian register.
result: FOUND, AND IT IS THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT: **NAA: BP25/1, ITALIAN MAZZA M**, Brisbane, Item ID 5041955, ACCESS OPEN -- «MAZZA [NEE NICOTRA], MARIA - Nationality: Italian - arrived Sydney 20 April 1962 on PHDCG». An Australian government file that states her MAIDEN NAME and gives an arrival this archive did not have. Alien registration files of this kind routinely carry a DATE AND PLACE OF BIRTH, which is exactly what twelve years of Piedimonte indexes have failed to establish. IT IS NOT DIGITISED -- paper, at the Brisbane reading room -- so it is a copy request, not a search. The NICOTRA name search returns 148 items; nothing else in the first twenty is this household, though «BP9/3, Nicotra, Teresa born 1895, arrived Brisbane on ORMONDE 16 September 1930» is a Brisbane Nicotra worth a second look.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1880 atto 66: the lead left standing is a son
scope: The 1880 M section carried «Mazza Gaetano -- 66» and the row was written up as a lead, not a finding, because Gaetano is a common name and the town holds three Mazza households. The act was then opened.
result: IT IS OURS, AND THE TEST WAS THE STREET AND THE MOTHER'S SURNAME. «Mazza Rosario, di anni trentadue, bracciante ... da BONANNO LEONARDA, industriosa, sua moglie ... VIA S. BASILIO ... il nome di GAETANO», born 5 May 1880. The other Rosario-and-Leonarda of this town lives in via Grotta Nicodemo and his wife is a Monacorso. SO THE NAMING CUSTOM HAS NOW CALLED TWO CHILDREN IN A ROW: Mariano in 1872 for the father's father, Gaetano in 1880 for the mother's father GAETANO BONANNO. The act-number map for this volume was banked on the way: two acts to the left page, one to the right, and act 66 sits on the right page of image 30.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1882 and 1883: fourteen consecutive years now, and no Orazio Mazza either
scope: Row 161, and a second question carried in the same read: the family tree dates ORAZIO MAZZA, son of Rosario and Leonarda, to 1883, and nothing has ever tested that.
result: FOURTEEN CONSECUTIVE YEARS, 1870-1883, AND NO MARIA NICOTRA. 1882's N section is NICOTRA NUNZIA 65, NUCIFORA ROSARIA 103, NICODEMO FRANCESCO 114. 1883's is NICOTRA ROSA 27, NUCIFORA LIBORIA 100, NUCIFORA MICHELE 189, NUCIFORA MARIANO 198, NUCIFORA ALFIO 201. AND THE SAME TWO PAGES ANSWER THE ORAZIO QUESTION: the 1883 M section holds MAZZA ROSARIA 117 and MAZZA VENERA 118 -- consecutive numbers, so possibly sisters or twins -- and NO ORAZIO. With the 1877 Orazio Mazza already shown to belong to the OTHER Rosario-and-Leonarda of the town, the tree's «Orazio Mazza, born 1883» has no birth act at Piedimonte in either year. He is not disproved, he is UNLOCATED, and the years between are unread.

source: Antenati — the Riveli di anime e di terre, Piedimonte 1747-1748: the whole index read
scope: Row 162, and the first time this archive has opened anything from the Deputazione del Regno. Container noPNme4, 73 images. IMAGES 1-14 ARE AN ALPHABETICAL INDEX with cut letter tabs down the fore-edge, and it is alphabetised BY GIVEN NAME, so the whole of it has to be read -- which it was, all fourteen openings, about eighty households.
result: THERE IS NO MAZZA AT PIEDIMONTE IN 1747. There are two MAZZEO: «Onofrio Mazzeo, folio 5» and «Silvestro Mazzeo, folio 29». Both were cropped at native resolution to be sure of the ending, and both read -EO. MAZZEO IS NOT MAZZA UNTIL SOMETHING SAYS IT IS -- Sicilian surname endings drift and the two may well be one family, but that is a hypothesis and this archive has been burned by exactly this kind of near-match before. THE REST OF THE TOWN IS STRIKINGLY CONTINUOUS: Pagano, Currenti, Grasso, Musumeci, Vasta, Puglisi, Torrisi, Sullo, Cadili, Vecchio, Barone, Moschella, di Mauro, Ricceri, Cassisi, Tomarchio, Zappala, Messina, Rinaldo, di Costa, Patane -- the same surnames that fill the birth indexes of the 1870s and 1880s. So the register is legible, the town is recognisable, and MAZZA IS NOT IN IT. That is consistent with what the nineteenth-century registers already said: no Mazza in the births of 1844 or 1846, two in 1845, four marriages in sixteen years.

source: Antenati — the two Mazzeo folios of the 1747 Piedimonte riveli, read in full
scope: Row 162. The index gave «Onofrio Mazzeo folio 5» and «Silvestro Mazzeo folio 29». The folio numbers are written in the top outer corner of each opening with an older number struck through, so the map falls out of five probes: FOLIO = IMAGE - 16 in container noPNme4.
result: BOTH READ, AND THE SURNAME IS SETTLED: MAZZEO, written four times across two folios in two hands, never Mazza. FOLIO 5: «Rivelo che Io ONOFRIO MAZZEO ... in virtu di Bando promulgato sotto li 30 Aprile 1747. ANIME: Notato Onofrio Mazzeo d'anni TRENTA; et CARMINA moglie; et GIUSEPPE figlio.» FOLIO 29: «Rivelo che Io SILVESTRO MAZZEO ... ANIME: M.ro Silvestro Mazzeo d'anni TRENTACINQUE; et MARIA moglie», followed by his house -- «un loggio terraneo di pietra a cruda, scagliato dentro e di fuori di calce, per proprio abitare, consistente in una stanza in piano». THE SHAPE OF A RIVELO, AND ITS LIMIT: «Rivelo che Io ...» naming the declarant and the bando, then ANIME, then BENI STABILI in close detail, then the dues. AT PIEDIMONTE ONLY THE HEAD'S AGE IS GIVEN -- the wife and the son are named and not aged -- so a rivelo here will not hand you a wife's or a child's birth year, which is the thing one hopes for. It gives the HOUSEHOLD and the HOUSE.

source: Antenati — Briatico relisted, and the listing is NOT complete
scope: Turning the Piedimonte lesson on the other deep line: `briatico-arks.tsv` holds EIGHTY registers, and nobody had checked whether that is the holding or just what was looked for. Prompted by CATERINA MELLUSO, born at Briatico in 1860 -- a wall on the ancestry chart with no parents and not one record against her.
result: BRIATICO HAS 555 REGISTERS, NOT EIGHTY. The result facets read «Archivio di Stato di Catanzaro (440)» and «Archivio di Stato di Vibo Valentia (115)». A listing at s_size=500 returned 500 of them and showed years running 1810 to 1930 WITH NOTHING BETWEEN 1859 AND 1910 -- which would put Caterina Melluso's 1860 birth and her marriage to Alfonso Prostamo beyond Antenati entirely. THAT IS NOT YET A FINDING AND IS RECORDED AS PART, NOT DONE. FIFTY-FIVE REGISTERS WERE NOT IN THE SAMPLE, and the ones held at Vibo Valentia rather than Catanzaro are exactly where a later series would sit. A 500-of-555 listing reported as a gap is the same error as a partial index section reported as a negative, and this archive has paid for that twice. s_size above 500 times out and the rate limiter closed the session before it could be finished by year probes. TO FINISH: one listing that reaches all 555, or year probes on 1860, 1880 and 1900.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1809 read entire: the first year of the register
scope: Rows 157 and 167. Container LD6vJel, twenty-five acts. The napoleonic form is BETTER than the restaurazione one for this: it names the groom, his age, his trade, his parents and THE BRIDE in one block, so a single crop band reads both spouses.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1813-1814 read entire, and an Arena household nobody had met
scope: Rows 157 and 167. Container 0MnkW4l, two years in one volume, forty-four acts, read groom by groom off the act head.

AND ACT 21 IS AN ARENA: DIEGO ARENA, thirty-seven, SARTORE, «figlio maggiore di DOMENICO ARENA, di anni SETTANTA, di professione BARBIERE, e di ANNA MELIDONI», marrying Maria Giuseppa Pontillo, sixteen, on 12 August 1813. DOMENICO ARENA WAS BORN ABOUT 1743, earlier than any Arena in this archive including Orazio, and he is a BARBER where the spine is sailors. NOTHING JOINS HIM TO FILIPPO and this archive has been caught by a shared given name before.

source: Antenati — Scilla, NINE consecutive marriage years read for a Donato: 1809-1817
scope: Row 167. The three indexed napoleonic years, 1810, 1811 and 1812, were read WHOLE rather than for one letter -- the 1811 and 1812 Tavole name both spouses AND all four parents, the 1810 indice names both spouses -- and 1809, 1813, 1814, 1815, 1816 and 1817 were read groom by groom off the act head.

source: Antenati — six Arena households at Scilla in the napoleonic years, and not one of them is Filippo's
scope: Row 157. Every napoleonic marriage year, 1809-1817, read for the surname ARENA on BOTH sides and in the parents' columns, which the 1811 and 1812 Tavole supply.
result: SIX ARENA, NONE OF THEM JOINED. As a GROOM: DIEGO ARENA, sartore, 1813 act 21, son of DOMENICO ARENA, barbiere, SEVENTY -- born about 1743, the earliest Arena in this archive. As BRIDES: GIACOMA ARENA (1809 act 10) and GIOVANNA ARENA (1812 act 10, daughter of CARLO ARENA and EUGENIA ATEJA). As MOTHERS: NATALINA ARENA (1811) and ANTONIA ARENA, dead before 1811, wife of Domenico Falcomata, whose two daughters marry in 1811 and 1812. SO THERE ARE AT LEAST THREE ARENA FATHERS AT SCILLA IN THIS DECADE -- DOMENICO the barber, CARLO, and ORAZIO who is Filippo's -- AND NOTHING CONNECTS THEM. That is the finding: not a line, but the shape of a surname in a town, and a warning against the join this archive would most like to make.

source: Queensland BDM — the whole NICOTRA and CASSANETI/CASSANITI index, swept by surname
scope: Row 161. The registrar's `downloadSearch` endpoint returns a whole result set as CSV in one GET. It refuses curl with a 403 and works from inside the site's own origin. Three spellings tried.
result: EIGHTEEN NICOTRA IN QUEENSLAND AND ONLY ONE IS OURS -- the 1963 death of «Maria Nicotra Mazza», parents JOHN NICOTRA and VENERA CASSANETI, which this archive already held. source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1821: FILIPPO ARENA'S BROTHER

source: Antenati — twelve Scilla marriage Tavole, 1820-1831, read at the A section

source: Antenati — seven more Scilla marriage Tavole, 1832-1838, and the year Orazio Arena died

source: Antenati — Scilla, Morti 1830 atto 64: ORAZIO ARENA, and his parents
scope: Row 169, opened this afternoon with a ten-year window. The death Tavole are the same instrument as the marriage ones -- surname order, a parents column, and the SPOUSE in it for a married person -- so a year costs one A-section crop. 1828 and 1829 were read first and hold other Arena.
result: FOUND IN THE SECOND YEAR, AND IT GIVES A GENERATION. The 1830 A section reads «ARENA ORAZIO -- Scilla -- MARINARO -- Mar.to MORABITO LETTERIA -- 12 Luglio». THREE THINGS: the death is exact to the hour; he was born about 1751, NINETEEN YEARS earlier than this archive had inferred from his sons' ages; and HIS PARENTS ARE NAMED -- FILIPPO ARENA and SANTA UNGARO, generation nine. The first son of Orazio is a Filippo, born 1793: the naming custom, confirmed by a record after the fact rather than used to make an identification.

source: Antenati — sixteen Scilla death containers banked, 1828-1844, and the 1838 A section read

source: The instruments, written down where a reader would look

source: Antenati — Scilla deaths 1838-1842 read at BOTH A and M for Litteria Morabito

source: Antenati — the 1714 Piedimonte riveli index read COMPLETE, and the running totals are what made it complete
scope: Row 162. Container qJkjONB, 283 images. Images 1 to 17 are a summary index -- «Nomi | Somme di Lordo | di Netto | Cagione di Riveli | folio» -- alphabetised BY GIVEN NAME, so there is no shortcut to a surname and all of it had to be read.
result: 142 HOUSEHOLDS, AND NO MAZZA AND NO MAZZEO IN ANY OF THEM. THE READING WAS ALMOST A PARTIAL ONE. Twelve index images were read first and two of them, p7 and p9, looked like blank versos at thumbnail size. THE RUNNING TOTALS SAID OTHERWISE: p6 closes at 1468 and p8 opens with a «riporto» of 2556, which is eight households nobody had read; p8 closes at 3774 and p10 opens at 4023. Both pages were fetched at full width and hold entries 73-80 and 106-108. A DOUBLE-ENTRY BOOK CHECKS ITSELF, AND THIS ONE CAUGHT A NEGATIVE THAT WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE BEEN ELEVEN HOUSEHOLDS SHORT. SO THE SEQUENCE AT PIEDIMONTE IS: 1714, no Mazzeo and no Mazza; 1747-1748, TWO MAZZEO and no Mazza; the civil registers from 1820, Mazza and no Mazzeo. THAT IS A SHAPE AND NOT A DESCENT, and it is recorded as one: a rivelo is a TAX RETURN and a household can be absent from one without being absent from the town.

source: The estate told about the Antenati name index
scope: Row 140. Not a Mazza finding but an estate one: Falco, Defranceschi and Lerena are reading Italian volumes the same way this archive was before it found the index.
result: SENT TO THE LANDING SITE FOR CIRCULATION, carrying the query form and the three cautions that each cost something here. THE QUERY: /search-nominative/?cognome=X&localita=Y&s_size=100, which returns acts with FATHER, MOTHER AND SPOUSE already extracted. THE CAUTIONS: the ACT TYPE DIFFERS BY COMUNE -- Scilla is indexed for deaths 1911-1943 and PIZZO FOR BIRTHS 1868-1903, so carrying «deaths only» across would produce a confident negative on a series indexed the other way round; «fq=» and «facets=» are SILENTLY IGNORED and return the unfiltered count, which looks like a successful filtered query; and ONLY ROWS WITH A p.morte VALUE ARE THE DECEASED -- the rest are relatives seen from inside somebody else's act, and reading them as deaths invents people with plausible names and dates. Also that «localita=» matches any place attached to a person, not the place of registration.

source: The Crupi given somewhere to live on the site

It carries the four things this archive knows about them that the family tree does not: that «ANGELA CUPO» is ANGELA CRUPI, born 20 December 1900; that she had THREE BROTHERS IN QUEENSLAND and nobody knew, all four registrations naming FRANCESCO CRUPI and MARIA VECCHIO; that PIETRO AND ANTONINO came into Brisbane together on the OTRANTO on 19 August 1930 as consecutive entries in the aliens register, and Angela followed on the VIMINALE in 1937 with two daughters; and that ANTONINO WAS INTERNED AT LOVEDAY, a boot repairer at Ingham with the fourth finger of his right hand deformed, born at PIEDIMONTE ETNEO -- the Mazza's own town. source: Antenati name index — ALL 69 Arena deaths at Scilla 1910-1943, pulled and read
scope: Rows 146 and 140. The query was re-run to TEST THE FORM this archive had just broadcast to three other archives -- an untested method note is untested code. It works, and it returns far more than the earlier sweep saw.

Coniuge Generosa Costa», and GIOVANNI, 31 March 1936, «Padre Antonio ... Coniuge Concetta Russo». FILIPPO AND GIUSEPPE, born 1852 and 1860, ARE IN NONE OF THE SIXTY-NINE.
