THE NINE MASCALI BIRTH YEARS OF 1839–1848 WERE READ AT THE JUNCTION, BEFORE THIS WAS KNOWN, AND ARE NOW MARKED PROVISIONAL — on the Mascali page and on the work list, row 180. Nothing FOUND is withdrawn: Alfio Nicotra and Carmela Sudieri are still in 1840 and 1847. Only the NEGATIVES are weaker than they were written, and saying so is cheaper than discovering it later.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Nati 1820, the first year Sicily registered anything
scope: Riposto Matrimoni 1844 put Nicotra Salvadore's birth at Giarre about 1815–1824 — a decade earlier than the eleven Giarre years already read. Sicilian civil registration begins in 1820 and there is nothing before it, so 1820 is the floor. Its N section was read whole, at full width.
result: TWO UNTITLED NICOTRA HOUSEHOLDS IN THE FIRST VOLUME. Atto 198, Nicotra Rosaria, of NICOTRA SIMONE and Marianna Dadone, 13 April. Atto 228, Nicotra Carmela, of NICOTRA ROSARIO and Rosa Providenza, 1 May. No Don, no Donna, written the way a labourer's name is written. SO «GIARRE'S ONLY NICOTRA IS A DOTTOR DON» WAS NEVER A FACT ABOUT GIARRE — IT WAS A FACT ABOUT ELEVEN YEARS OF IT, and this archive had let the eleven stand for the town. THE SECOND FATHER IS CALLED ROSARIO AND IT IS NOT HIM: Giovanni's father was a working bracciante in October 1872 and a man fathering a child in May 1820 would be past seventy-five by then. It is the generation a grandson is named after, which is naming custom, which this archive already files as weak evidence. THE NAME IS RECORDED AND THE JOIN IS NOT MADE. The test is Salvadore Nicotra's own birth act, which would say whether Alfio, Simone and Rosario are brothers. Also in the same section and not Nicotra: Nicolosi Pietro, Nota Alessandro, Nucifora Alfio.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Matrimoni 1835–1846 and Nati 1821–1826: blocked by the rate limiter, not by the register
scope: The obvious next sweeps after Giarre 1820: the remaining early birth years, which would hold Salvadore Nicotra's own act, and the Giarre marriage Tavole, where Rosario Nicotra × Venera Murabito would be if he married in the town his son was born in.
result: NOT A NEGATIVE AND NOT A WALL — UNREAD. Twenty-one ark→container lookups were attempted and ONE returned before the throttle took the rest: every other one came back with this archive's known 520-byte, HTTP 403, «no Nessun risultato» signature. CORRECTED FROM YESTERDAY'S NOTE: a three-second pause between lookups does NOT keep you under the limiter, it only raises the batch from two or three to about twenty-eight. THE LIMITER IS CUMULATIVE. And a fifteen-minute wait after a lock was NOT enough — exactly one fetch got through before it closed again, so recovery is gradual rather than a clean reset. THE IMAGES THEMSELVES ARE NEVER THROTTLED; it is only the HTML page that carries a container id. So this is a queue to work through at about twenty-five containers a session, not a problem with Giarre.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Matrimoni 1844, and the Don Alfio who is «of S. Giovanni» in one register and «of Giarre» in another
scope: The Giarre marriage containers came through after the throttle cleared. 1844 was opened first because that is the year Nicotra Salvadore married at Riposto, and a brother marrying at home would sit beside him. The N section was read at full width.
result: TWO N ENTRIES AND THE IMPORTANT ONE IS NOT ROSARIO. Atto 54, 19 August 1844: NICOTRA D.r D. ALFIO, PATRIA GIARRE, son of Nicotra D. Giuseppe and CALTABIANO D. GIOACHINA, marrying Consoli D. Antonina — the couple whose Salvatore appears in the birth index in November 1846 and again in January 1848. Also atto 8, Noscia Mro Ignazio × Castorina Anna, which is not a Nicotra. THE FINDING IS A JOIN THIS ARCHIVE HAD REFUSED TO MAKE. Riposto Matrimoni 1838 atto 15 marries «Nicotra D. Alfio, son of FU D. GIUSEPPE and D. GIOACHINA CATTABIANO» to Ligresti D. Angela. THE SAME TWO PARENTS. It is ONE MAN, widowed and remarried across two comuni, and the household file said in September that whether he was Giarre's Don Alfio remarried «is not decided here». It is decided now, by the parents and not by the name. AND THE TWO REGISTERS GIVE HIM TWO BIRTHPLACES: Riposto wrote his patria «S. GIOVANNI», Giarre wrote «GIARRE». SAN GIOVANNI MONTEBELLO IS A FRAZIONE OF GIARRE, so both are true. THAT IS THE THIRD READING OF GIOVANNI NICOTRA'S PROBLEM, DOCUMENTED IN HIS OWN SURNAME: a man of this district can be «nato a Giarre» in one register and entered under a frazione's name in another. It does not find Giovanni; it makes his case possible without either of his declared ages being wrong. STILL TO READ: Giarre Matrimoni 1835-1843 and 1845-1846, containers banked. THE REACH: one year of one comune's marriage index, at the only section that could hold the surname.

source: Antenati — the MASCALI riveli of 1616 opened: the oldest source in this archive, and it has a name index
scope: Forty-six Mascali volumes sit at PALERMO rather than Catania and are not civil registration at all: they are RIVELI DI BENI E DI ANIME, household returns made to the Sicilian parliament, and the earliest is 1616 — two centuries before any register this archive has read and the oldest source of any kind in it. The first volume was opened to find out what it is.
result: 546 IMAGES, AND IT OPENS WITH AN ALPHABETICAL NAME INDEX, WITH THE LETTER TABS CUT INTO THE FORE-EDGE OF THE BOOK — B C D E F G I L M N P R S T V are visible in the photograph, AND THERE IS AN N. Each line gives a name and a folio number. THE CATCH, AND IT DECIDES HOW THIS IS SEARCHED: THE INDEX IS ORDERED BY FORENAME, NOT BY SURNAME. The A pages run Antonino lo Xuto, Antonino Puliseva, Antonio Barbagallo, Antonino Gagliano, Adamo Mangano, Alfonso di Lonardo, Aloisia lo Castro, Agata Grasso, Alfio Pinnisi, Alfio Musumeci, Antonino Musumeci and so on. So the N tab leads to Natale and Nicolo, NOT to Nicotra, and finding a surname means reading the index through rather than jumping to a letter. That is still perhaps twenty images instead of five hundred and forty-six, which is the difference between a task and a wall. THE SURNAMES ARE THE SAME ONES THE 1840s REGISTERS ARE FULL OF — Barbagallo, Musumeci, Finocchiaro, Grasso, Gagliano, Pinnisi, Strano, Arcidiacono, Puliseo — which says the population is continuous across two hundred years even though no line of descent is drawn. NO NICOTRA SEEN YET AND NONE LOOKED FOR PROPERLY: one opening of the index was read. THE REACH: this says what the instrument is and nothing about who is in it.

source: Trove API v3 — the naturalisation gazettes, swept by surname now that a key exists
scope: David obtained a Trove API key on 27 September, valid to December 2026, which closes work-list row 153 and unblocks rows 7 and 79. Row 79 had failed on the TOOL and not the source: Trove's search page accepts a query, echoes it back, throws inside its own vendor bundle on a storage API the browser pane does not provide, and never paints a result list. The API needs no JavaScript. Seven surnames swept in the newspaper category, which includes the Commonwealth of Australia Gazette.
result: SEVEN NATURALISATION ENTRIES, IN A SOURCE THAT HAD BEEN BLOCKED FOR EIGHT DAYS. PROSTAMO: Angela and Antonino Giacomo, gazetted 16 November 1961; Assunta, 3 November 1966. POLISTENA: Maria Luisa, 22 January 1959; Maria, 13 March 1969; Annunziato, 20 March 1969. MELLUSO: Francesco, 6 July 1961. ALL ARE CANDIDATES AND NONE IS A JOIN — data/trove-gazette.tsv says so row by row. A certificate-of-naturalisation notice in this gazette is a NAME IN AN ALPHABETICAL LIST and nothing else: no birth date, no address, no former nationality in these notices, so there is nothing in them to disambiguate two men of one name with. ANGELA PROSTAMO IS THE ONE NEW NAME; the rest match people the export already holds. AND ONE DISCREPANCY WORTH KEEPING: this archive already held «Maria Assunta's gazettal of 4 JULY 1966»; the notice found here is 3 NOVEMBER 1966 and prints ASSUNTA without the Maria. Two notices or two readings, and which has not been established. TWO THINGS THE API WILL NOT DO, both of which look like absence. (1) IT DOES NOT SERVE ARTICLE TEXT FOR GOVERNMENT GAZETTE NOTICES: `include=articletext` is accepted and silently ignored on /result AND on /newspaper/<id>, and `snippet` comes back empty, which reads exactly like an article with no words in it. The OCR is on the public page at nla.gov.au/nla.news-article<id> and tools/trove.py fetches it there. (2) THE DEFAULT SEARCH IS NOT EXACT: «Anile» returns 5,834,914 results — it is matching inside longer words, which is this estate's own «short token inside a long word» trap arriving in a new source, and that surname needs a phrase query before any of it means anything. THE OCR IS ALSO TWO COLUMNS READ ACROSS: entries print «Surname, Given Names» and flatten into «Prineas, Panagiotis Prostamo, Angela Prostamo, Antonmo Giacomo Przybylo, Jozef», so the given name after a surname belongs with THAT surname and «Antonmo» is Antonino. THE REACH: seven surnames, the newspaper and gazette category, certificate-of-naturalization notices only. Trove's newspapers largely stop at 1955 and the gazette runs to 1973, so this answers for the naturalisation window and for nothing later. THE 1942 INTERNMENTS (row 7) ARE NOT YET SWEPT.

source: Trove API — the 1942 internments: two named internees, and the newspapers do not name them
scope: Work-list row 7, unblocked the same day as the API key. The NAA has already given two named internees in this family — ROSARIO MAZZA (MP1103/1 Q8110, born 20 February 1899) and MARIO CRUPI, both held at LOVEDAY in South Australia from 18 August 1942 to 30 December 1943. The row's hope was that «internees' names sometimes printed». Four phrase queries: each man by name, Loveday with internment, and Mazza against internee and Queensland.
result: THE NEWSPAPERS DO NOT NAME EITHER MAN AS AN INTERNEE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. «Rosario Mazza» returns FOURTEEN articles, every one of them Queensland and none of them about internment: a wine overcharging fine at Brisbane in March 1947, a warning on dirty premises in September 1947, an eviction case in 1952, a Gordonvale police court in 1935. THEY MAY WELL BE HIS — he was released in December 1943 and a Brisbane tradesman in the late forties fits — but a name in a court report is not an identification and none of them is attached. «Mario Crupi» returns SIX, all in the right country: Innisfail, Cairns, Tully, Townsville, which is exactly where this archive already places the Crupi brothers. None mentions internment either. WHAT TROVE DOES HOLD IS THE CAMP, NOT THE ROLL. «Loveday» with internment returns 1,085 articles and they are good ones — «ITALIAN INTERNEES AT LOVEDAY: First Train Load Arrives», Murray Pioneer, 12 June 1941; preparations at the camp in May 1941; the Italians leaving in 1948. The South Australian papers covered the camp's existence closely and its inmates anonymously. SO THE ROW'S PREMISE IS TESTED AND FALSE FOR THESE TWO MEN. Internee names were not routinely printed, and the NAA file remains the only place either man is named. THE REACH: Trove's digitised newspapers, four phrase queries, both men by full name. Trove's newspaper run largely ends in 1954, which COVERS the 1942–43 internment window completely — this is not a coverage gap, it is an absence in the source.

source: Trove — every Australian person this archive holds, searched by name, and where the source ends
scope: Asked whether Trove has anything left. Rather than guess: every Mazza this archive places in Australia searched by full name, plus the nine other surnames, plus the remaining naturalisation sweep. Phrase form `text:"..."`, established below.
result: SIXTEEN QUEENSLAND HITS ACROSS EVERY AUSTRALIAN MAZZA THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS, and most of the names return NOTHING: Michele, Ignazio, Venera Mazza, Alfonso Prostamo, Caterina Melluso, Giovanni Polistena are all zero. TWO ARE WORTH HAVING AND BOTH ARE BEHIND A WALL. (1) SEBASTIANO MAZZA, News-Mail (Bundaberg), 6 JULY 1962, headed «THREE NEW CITIZENS», snippet «Supported by friends and relatives, three former Italian citizens received certificates of...» — A NATURALISATION CEREMONY REPORT. (2) SEBASTIANO MAZZA again, same paper, 28 SEPTEMBER 1963, «Family Notices». Also CONCETTA MAZZA, a Queensland «Family Notices» of 17 FEBRUARY 1958. ALL THREE CARRY `status: currently unavailable`. Trove indexes these post-1955 Queensland papers and will not serve the text — the article pages 404 at both nla.gov.au/nla.news-article<id> and trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/<id>, though the search matched inside them. THIS IS A COPYRIGHT WALL, NOT AN ABSENCE, and the distinction matters: the words exist, are indexed, and are reachable another way. About 13 per cent of Nicotra hits carry the same flag. AND THE 1962 CEREMONY CONTRADICTS SOMETHING THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS. Row 105 reasons that Sebastiano Mazza was naturalised BEFORE 1959, because only British subjects could be enrolled and he is on the 1959 Queensland roll at Wacol. A naturalisation ceremony at BUNDABERG in July 1962 does not fit that, and Bundaberg is three hundred and fifty kilometres from Wacol. Either it is a different Sebastiano Mazza, or one of the two readings is wrong. NOT RESOLVED HERE and not attached to him. THE PHRASE FORM, because the obvious one does not work: `"Anile"` in quotes returns 5,834,914 — IDENTICAL to the unquoted total, so quoting does not bind. `text:"Anile"` returns 41,162, a 99.3 per cent cut. Controls run alongside: `Zzqqxxwv` returns 0 quoted and unquoted, so a zero here is real, and `Catania` returns 30,090. THE REACH: Trove's digitised newspapers and the Commonwealth Gazette, every Australian person in this archive by full name. It does NOT answer for anyone who never reached Australia, and it does not answer for the post-1955 Queensland press, which it indexes and withholds.

source: Trove — the categories that are not newspapers, and the Queensland wills hiding in them
scope: Asked a second time whether Trove was finished, and the honest answer was that I had only searched ONE OF ITS CATEGORIES. Rows 7, 79 and 153 are all about newspapers and the Commonwealth Gazette; Trove also aggregates books, images, magazines, music, people, research and «diaries, letters and archives», the last of which carries ITEM-LEVEL RECORDS FROM STATE ARCHIVES. Eleven surnames across eight categories, with the Zzqqxxwv control run in every one of them.
result: TROVE IS NOT FINISHED, AND THE THING IT WAS HIDING IS BETTER THAN ANYTHING IN THE NEWSPAPERS. The `diary` category surfaces QUEENSLAND STATE ARCHIVES item records, and four of them are NICOTRA WILLS: SALVATORE PHILIP (1955, ITM938108), LEONARDA (1962), VINCENZO (1965), FILIPPO (1966) — all «Part of series Supreme Court (Northern) Ecclesiastical Files (Wills) (S6220)», all held at QSA, all marked OPEN ACCESS. A will file names the deceased, the date of death, the address, the occupation, the executors and the beneficiaries, which is usually the whole household. ALL FOUR ARE TOWNSVILLE DISTRICT, AND NORTH QUEENSLAND HAS ALREADY COME UP TWICE IN THIS SWEEP: the only two Nicotra family notices in the newspapers are the Evening Advocate (INNISFAIL), 1 May and 17 September 1953, and the Lands Department holds three Nicotra land files for Innisfail and Cardwell Shire. THERE IS A NORTH QUEENSLAND NICOTRA CLUSTER and this archive has never looked at it. WHETHER IT IS MARIA NICOTRA'S FAMILY IS COMPLETELY UNKNOWN — she died at Brisbane in 1963, four hundred kilometres south — and nothing here is attached to anybody. ALSO FOUND: «Naturalisation - Central District - MAZZA, James, 1898» at Rockhampton, half a century before this family reached Australia and recorded so nobody chases it twice. And court files under CASSANITI and MURABITO — both surnames off the Nicotra line — but dated 2014, 2015 and 2018, which is modern and touches the living, so they are named here and not pursued. AND A CORRECTION TO THE SAME DAY'S WORK. This archive was told a few hours earlier that Trove could be closed. THAT ADVICE WAS WRONG, and wrong in a way worth writing down: the sweep was thorough inside one category and never asked what the other seven held. A source is not exhausted because the part of it you know about is. THE REACH: eight Trove categories, eleven surnames, controls in each. It does not reach anyone who never came to Australia.

source: Antenati — Giarre Nati 1827 and 1828, the annual Tavole read whole
scope: Giarre (Catania), Stato civile della restaurazione. 1827: ark an_ua68985, segnatura 15927, container 5xe4lba, 175 images, Tavola at folios 170-173. 1828: ark an_ua68986, segnatura 15928, container wRGJ3ja, 237 images, Tavola at folios 229-230. Archivio di Stato di Catania. Both Tavole read from the first heading to the last rather than by junction, because a junction negative is unsafe where section order cannot be assumed.
result: A NULL ON NICOTRA IN BOTH. The N heading is ruled and left blank in each year, with O blank beneath it, then P opens at Pafumi act 34 (1827) and Pennisi act 12 (1828). The first MURABITO households this archive has found anywhere turned up instead — three of them across the two years, one of which names a daughter Venera in 1827 and another daughter in 1828. Murabito is a common Giarre surname, so «Venera Murabito of Giarre» is ordinary rather than remarkable. The 1827 Venera is NOT Rosario Nicotra's wife: born 1827 she would have been fourteen when Giovanni was born about 1841.

source: Antenati — Mascali, whether a 1844 volume exists in any series
scope: Mascali (Catania), the whole holding: 498 results, 498 distinct arks, facet totals agreeing, so a complete listing and not a sample at the page-size ceiling. Every series checked for 1844 — Nati, Morti, Matrimoni, Nati esposti, Matrimoni processetti, the memorandum notificazioni, and Diversi.
result: MASCALI HAS NO 1844 IN ANY RESTAURAZIONE SERIES. The run goes 1843 then 1845 throughout, and both counters step by exactly one across the gap — ark an_ua70313 to an_ua70314, Catania segnatura 16777 to 16778 — where every other year steps by one per year. The year was never deposited rather than dropped from a listing. GIARRE HAS 1844, so this is Mascali's hole and not a regional one. Any Mascali negative spanning 1844 is complete without it, and no search should be planned for it.

source: Antenati — which endpoints the rate limiter actually governs
scope: Tested across a working day while the site was refusing traffic: the ark landing pages (antenati.cultura.gov.it/ark:/12657/...), the search listing (/ricerca/), the IIIF image service (iiif-antenati.cultura.gov.it) and the container manifest (dam-antenati.cultura.gov.it/antenati/containers/<id>/manifest).
result: THE THROTTLE IS ON THE HTML, NOT ON THE IMAGES. Ark pages and /ricerca/ returned a blanket 403 all day, including to an ordinary browser, while the IIIF image service and the container manifest served every request without complaint. So a volume whose CONTAINER is already recorded can be read in full during a throttle; only the ark-to-container lookup is blocked. That is the argument for banking container ids in the ark tables as they are found. Also: asking IIIF for a width greater than the image's own returns a 403 whose BODY IS AN HTML ERROR PAGE, which will be saved as a .jpg by anything that does not check.

source: Antenati — Mascali Morti 1882, and the early M of 1881
scope: Mascali (Catania), Stato civile italiano. 1882: ark an_ua81729, segnatura 8853, container 0JbrlJG, 53 images, Indice Annuale at folio 40. 1881: ark an_ua81728, segnatura 8852, container LPR9gW8, 63 images, index at folio 38. Both indexes read whole, M and N, across the paired exposures described in the row below.
result: BOTH NULL ON NICOTRA'S ROSARIO AND ON MURABITO. 1882 holds three N entries — Neri Maria 75, Nucifora Filippo 82, Nicolosi Enna 106 — and no Murabito in M. 1881 holds five — Nicotra Nunziato 2, Nicotra Salvatore 14, Neri Salvatore 16, Neri Maria 37, Nucifora Maria 61 — and its EARLY M, previously unread behind the card, holds no Murabito either. That matters because an Italian death index files a married woman under her maiden surname, so the M section is where a Venera Murabito would appear and half of 1881's had never been looked at. 1882 had been recorded as unreadable and was not.

source: Antenati — the DUPLICATA card is moved between exposures, so a covered page is not a lost one
scope: Observed in two Mascali death volumes at the Archivio di Stato di Catania, containers 0JbrlJG (1882, images 51 and 52) and LPR9gW8 (1881, images 61 and 62). Method note, not a family finding.
result: WHERE A BLACK «DUPLICATA» CARD COVERS HALF AN OPENING, LOOK AT THE ADJACENT IMAGE. The opening is photographed TWICE and the card is moved between exposures — once resting on the left-hand page, once on the right — so the two images together give every column. The card identifies the archive's duplicate copy; it is not damage and it is not a redaction. A session that reads one image and stops will record a year as unreadable when it is fully legible, and that is exactly what happened here: Mascali Morti 1882 sat as «hidden behind the cover sheet» for a day, and 1881 had half its M section written off the same way. Neither volume has a second copy to fall back on, so the mistake would have been permanent. Separately: the volume's back cover may carry the archive's own condition labels — PAG. ONDULATE, PAG. MACCHIATA, PAG. TRASPARENTE, TUTTO IL VOLUME, IMPOSSIBILE FARE DI MEGLIO — which describe the paper and say nothing about whether the index can be read.

source: Antenati — Mascali Nati 1873, 1874, 1876 and 1877, the annual indexes and two acts
scope: Mascali (Catania), Stato civile italiano, Archivio di Stato di Catania. 1873 ark an_ua81752 segn 8759 container wE72Q9W (70 images, index folio 56, act 145 at image 60); 1874 an_ua81753 / 8760 / w68j9AQ (70, folio 63); 1876 an_ua81755 / 8762 / 5gKnx4N (85, folio 70); 1877 an_ua81756 / 8763 / LpAxl61 (78, folio 66, act 8 at image 6). N section read whole in each year; two acts fetched in full. 1873 and 1874 carry a PATERNITÀ column in the index and 1876 and 1877 do not, which decides whether a father can be had without fetching the act.
result: THE TARGET HOUSEHOLD FOUND, AND TWO MORE BESIDE IT. Mascali Nati 1873 atto 145 is the birth of VENERA NICOTRA to GIOVANNI NICOTRA DI ROSARIO, lavorante, and VENERA CASSANITI FU GAETANO, at contrada Nocille — «di» Rosario and not «fu», in an act that writes «fu» for the wife's dead father four lines below, so the father was alive in December 1873. 1874, 1876 and 1877 hold no further child of that couple, which fits the two births already known. Three other Nicotra households at Mascali: GAETANO x CARMELA CAVALLARO of Nunziata (daughters 1874 and 1877, the second read in full), GIUSEPPE FU ANGELO (a witness Giovanni chose himself), and an ALFIO fathering a child in 1873. Act 4 of 1877, Nicotra Mariano, remains unread. A namesake worth knowing: TWO Maria Nicotras born at Mascali twenty months apart, 1874 to Gaetano and 1875 to Giovanni.

source: Antenati — Giarre Nati 1827-1837, closing the 1820-1848 run
scope: Giarre (Catania), Stato civile della restaurazione, Archivio di Stato di Catania. Eleven annual Tavole, each read from the first heading to the last rather than by junction — 1834's alphabet runs P, Q, V, S, so junction negatives are unsafe in these volumes. Arks an_ua68985 to an_ua68995, containers 5xe4lba, wRGJ3ja, 5vxY4ly, LpA8n1Z, wQ8J9vY, 5GE26Nx, 5vxY4Kl, Lapd1WA, 5dZj6aK, LqJro1B, wbr2VZX. With the years already held this COMPLETES Giarre births 1820-1848: twenty-nine consecutive years, no gaps.
result: A NULL ON NICOTRA ACROSS THE WHOLE DECADE, and the completed run turns it into a finding. Giarre's ordinary Nicotra appear in 1820 and 1821 — four households, two of them headed by a ROSARIO — and then disappear from the birth registers for twenty-four years, after which the only Nicotra left is a titled «Dottor Don» line in 1846 and 1848. The N section is ruled and blank in six of the eleven years and ABSENT ALTOGETHER in four; the one N entry in 1836 is a Nicciò. GIOVANNI NICOTRA, whose 1872 marriage act says «nato a GIARRE» and whose age puts his birth between about 1841 and about 1847, is in none of it, and neither is a sibling. Either the birth went unregistered, or «Giarre» meant a frazione or the district rather than the comune, or he was born elsewhere. SIX MURABITO HOUSEHOLDS were recorded in passing, three of them against the one name Giuseppe Murabito with three different wives, and TWO daughters called Venera — so Venera Murabito is an ordinary Giarre name and cannot be pinned on the name alone.

source: Antenati — Mascali Morti 1873-1893 swept whole, and Rosario Nicotra found
scope: Mascali (Catania), Stato civile italiano, Archivio di Stato di Catania. All 21 annual death indexes 1873-1893, the whole digitised range. Every index read for MURABITO in the M section as well as NICOTRA in the N, because an Italian death index files a married woman under her MAIDEN surname. Most volumes needed BOTH paired exposures: the archive's black DUPLICATA card covers one page of an opening in one image and the other page in the next.
result: ROSARIO NICOTRA FOUND, atto 35 of 1890, read in the original: «è morto NICOTRA ROSARIO, di anni NOVANTA CIRCA, CONTADINO, residente in Mascali, NATO IN GIARRE, da fu SIMONE, e da fu MUSUMECI MARIANNA, MARITO DI MURABITO VENERA», died 4 April 1890 at contrada Montargi. Born about 1800 AT GIARRE — which is very likely why his son's 1872 marriage act says «nato a Giarre» — with a trade, a death, a wife named beside him and TWO PARENTS the archive did not have, a seventh generation. «MARITO», not «vedovo», so VENERA MURABITO OUTLIVED HIM; she appears in none of these 21 indexes, and 1893 is where Antenati's Mascali stops, so her death is beyond the digitised range and needs the comune or a certificate. Also found: the first MURABITO at Mascali rather than Giarre — BARTOLO, bracciale, born Mascali, son of a Paolo, died 1885 atto 4, declared 106; and SALVATORE Murabito 1886 atto 78. Four other Nicotra households, and two 1883 Nicotra infant deaths proved by their acts to belong to other families.

source: Antenati — Mascali Matrimoni 1835-1847 and Riposto Matrimoni 1830-1846, swept whole
scope: Mascali and Riposto (Catania), Archivio di Stato di Catania. Mascali's thirteen marriage Tavole 1835-1847 (1844 was never deposited) and Riposto's seventeen 1830-1846. MASCALI'S SECTIONS ARE NOT IN ALPHABETICAL ORDER — 1847 runs C, N, M; 1841 and 1835 put V before S — so every volume was read heading by heading and no junction negative was taken.
result: NO NICOTRA GROOM AT MASCALI IN THIRTEEN YEARS; four of its Tavole have no N section at all. Riposto 1830 holds the ONLY Nicotra groom found in any marriage index across three towns and 118 read years: atto 12, «D. FRANCESCO NICOTRA di anni venticinque, NATO IN GIARRE, CALZOLAJO, figlio di D. GIUSEPPE e di ROSARIA MISANO di anni sessantaquattro», marrying Maria Sapienza of Riposto. The «D.» is Don and the trade is artisan, so this is the TITLED Giarre Nicotra and not the bracciante line — but Rosaria Misano born about 1766 makes them the earliest Nicotra generation reached anywhere. NOTE FOR ANYONE USING THESE INDEXES: they list by the GROOM'S surname only, so a bride of the name will not appear under her own letter.

source: Antenati — MASCALI Matrimoni 1820–1829, the decade Rosario would have married in
scope: Mascali (Catania), Archivio di Stato di Catania. All ten marriage Tavole of 1820–1829, each read from its first section heading to its last rather than at the M-to-next-letter junction. Containers w992969, wlG7G22, 57PKPmX, wXrJr7v, w68l8zb, wRGbGWQ, 0A4p4mg, 0Jb9beG, 0Jb9brG, 0ZJeJRa. Every year checked against the register's own closing line, which states the act count in words, so each reading is a whole table and not a half: venticinque, undici, sedici, ventiquattro, trentuno, trentuno, quindici, and the rest.
result: NO NICOTRA GROOM IN ANY OF THE TEN YEARS. Seven have no N heading ruled at all; three carry a single N entry and none is a Nicotra — NICIFORA Leonardo (1824 atto 22), NICIFORA Mariano (1825 atto 17), NICOLOSI Salvadore (1827 atto 10). 1827 IS THE ONE TO REMEMBER: ITS N SECTION SITS AFTER THE P. The headings run C, F, G, M, P, N, R, T, V, so a reader who stopped at the M–P junction would have called the year empty and been wrong. That is the third independent proof that MASCALI'S SECTIONS ARE NOT ALPHABETICAL — 1847 runs C, N, M and 1841 and 1835 put V before S. One find attached to nobody: the 1825 groom's mother is written NICOTRA MARIA, a Nicotra woman born by about 1785, a generation above Rosario; a shared surname in one town is not a link. This closes Mascali as the place Rosario Nicotra married. His 1890 death act says NATO IN GIARRE, and Giarre is where the marriage must now be looked for.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Matrimoni 1820–1829, the decade in Rosario's birthplace
scope: Giarre (Catania), Archivio di Stato di Catania. All ten marriage Tavole 1820–1829, each read from its first ruled letter to its last. Containers LqJrKnB, 5VKXP9J, wrdrmWX, 5VKXPmV, LydYKx1, wbr2Ron, wrdrmey, Lme8RKK, LoYEKVR, LeGQRZD. Opened because Rosario Nicotra's 1890 Mascali death act says NATO IN GIARRE and Mascali's own marriage decade had just come back empty.
result: TWO NICOTRA GROOMS IN 1820 — the first found in any Giarre marriage index. ATTO 30, 1 May: NICOTRA SALVADORE x Strano Giuseppa, son of NICOTRA CIRINO and PELLINI MARIA. ATTO 80, 31 July: NICOTRA GIUSEPPE x Cattabiano Rosa, son of NICOTRA MASTRO SEBASTIANO and TORNABENE CARMELA. Neither is Rosario, who was about twenty that year; these are two Nicotra HOUSEHOLDS of Giarre standing in the same generation as his father Simone. The acts themselves are in the same volume and are not yet read. THE OTHER NINE YEARS GIVE NOTHING: 1822 and 1824 hold a single N entry each and both are NICOLOSI, 1821 has no N heading at all, and 1823, 1825, 1826, 1827, 1828 and 1829 have the heading RULED AND BLANK. FOR ANYONE USING THESE INDEXES: Giarre's clerks rule every letter whether or not it carries an entry — 1823 rules A·B, D·E, N, O and Q all empty — so a blank heading at Giarre is a positive statement of absence. That is the opposite of Mascali, whose clerks file out of order and whose silences prove nothing. CAVEAT ON 1820: the Tavola's first leaf (entries 1–56, letters A–L) was never photographed; the index is strictly alphabetical and the N section is bounded by M before and O after, but the year is not a whole reading and is not recorded as one.

source: Antenati — RIPOSTO Matrimoni 1821–1829, the decade completed
scope: Riposto (Catania), Archivio di Stato di Catania. All nine marriage Tavole 1821–1829 — Riposto's civil registers begin in 1821 — each read from its first ruled letter to «Fine». Containers w68qppe, w99mlP6, 5GEmr1N, wrd7kap, wE71q3d, LqJm8qP, wlG6nqY, 5YGADzP, wbrBz3Z. Every year checked against the register's own closing line, which states the act count in words.
result: THE N HEADING IS RULED IN ALL NINE YEARS AND CARRIES NOTHING IN ANY OF THEM. No Nicotra, and no N entry of any surname, in the whole decade. THESE ARE THE STRONGEST NEGATIVES IN THE SWEEP, because Riposto's clerks rule every letter of the alphabet whether or not anything falls under it — 1828 rules twenty letters and only seven carry an entry — so a blank N is written down rather than omitted. Two years prove their own heading placement: in 1827 and 1829 the letter directly beneath the blank N is O, carrying OLIVERI Teodoro and OLIVIERI Mariano, so the blank line is the N section and not a mis-set heading. 1821 is flagged «Faded Document» by the archive and its ruled letters were read as a full-resolution IIIF crop rather than called from the page view. WITH THIS THE 1820s ARE CLOSED IN ALL THREE TOWNS — twenty-nine Tavole across Mascali, Giarre and Riposto — and the decade yielded exactly one thing: the two Nicotra grooms of Giarre 1820.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Matrimoni 1820, atti 30 and 80 read in the original
scope: Giarre (Catania), container LqJrKnB, images 61 and 163. The two Nicotra marriages the 1820 Tavola had just turned up, pulled from the Tavola's act numbers to the acts themselves so the index entries became documents.
result: BOTH ACTS READ IN FULL, and they give the generation this archive had never reached at Giarre. ATTO 30 (21 April 1820): SALVADORE NICOTRA, DI ANNI TRENTASEI COMPIUTI, NATO IN QUESTO COMUNE, CONTADINO, figlio di FU CIRINO, DI ANNI OTTANTA, UN TEMPO CONTADINO, e di FU MARIA — marrying Giuseppa Strano of the S. Leonardello quarter, daughter of fu Giuseppe and Rosa Vitale; church marriage 22 April, documents foglio 271. ATTO 80 (24 July 1820): GIUSEPPE NICOTRA, DI ANNI VENTITRE COMPIUTI, NATO IN QUESTO COMUNE, CONTADINO, figlio di MAESTRO SEBASTIANO, DI ANNI CINQUANTA, FALEGNAME, e di CARMELA TORNABENE, DI ANNI CINQUANTA — marrying Rosa Cattabiano of the S. Alfio quarter, daughter of fu Carmelo and Maria Musumeci; church marriage 31 July, documents foglio 564. SO CIRINO NICOTRA WAS BORN ABOUT 1740 AND WAS DEAD BY APRIL 1820, AND MASTRO SEBASTIANO NICOTRA WAS BORN ABOUT 1770 AND WAS ALIVE IN JULY 1820. Rosario Nicotra was born about 1800 at Giarre to SIMONE and Marianna Musumeci; Sebastiano stands in Simone's own generation and Cirino one above it, and Giuseppe is Rosario's near-exact contemporary in the same town and trade. NOTHING IS ATTACHED — Giuseppe is not Rosario's brother, their parents being different couples, and whether Simone was Cirino's son or Sebastiano's brother is not established by these acts. Filed as question 19. THE NEXT MOVE IS GIARRE NATI 1796-1800, which would give Giuseppe's and Rosario's baptisms with their fathers named and settle it in one pair of acts.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Nati 1820 atto 198, the Simone Nicotra act read in the original
scope: Giarre (Catania), container 03PBQXV, canvas 201. The 1820 birth index had recorded «atto 198 Nicotra Rosaria, of NICOTRA SIMONE and Marianna Dadone» since the Giarre birth sweep. SIMONE is the name of Rosario Nicotra's father and the deepest name this archive holds, so the act itself was pulled to see what it gives.
result: «È COMPARSO SIMONE NICOTRA, DI ANNI QUARANTAQUATTRO, DI PROFESSIONE CONTADINO, DOMICILIATO NEL QUARTIERE S. ALFIO DI QUESTO COMUNE ... LA STESSA È NATA DA MARIANNA DAIDONE SUA LEGITTIMA MOGLIE, DI ANNI QUARANTA», 15 April 1820, declaring a daughter ROSARIA born on the 13th, baptised on the 24th; documents at foglio 263. SO THIS SIMONE NICOTRA WAS BORN ABOUT 1776, HIS WIFE ABOUT 1780, AND THEY LIVED IN THE S. ALFIO QUARTER OF GIARRE. THE CONFLICT, STATED PLAINLY: Rosario Nicotra was born about 1800 AT GIARRE and his 1890 Mascali death act names his parents as fu SIMONE and fu MUSUMECI MARIANNA. This Simone is a contadino at Giarre of exactly the right age to have fathered Rosario at twenty-four, and the wife's FORENAME MATCHES EXACTLY — but her surname is written DAIDONE here and MUSUMECI there. Both were read at full resolution off IIIF crops and neither is a strained reading. He is the strongest candidate this archive has ever had for Rosario's father and HE IS NOT ATTACHED TO HIM; a forename and a town are not a link. Filed as question 19. A CORRECTION RECORDED WITH IT: the previous note said the next move was Giarre Nati 1796-1800. NO SUCH REGISTER EXISTS — every Giarre civil series begins in 1820, the first year Sicily registered, and earlier births are parish records not held by Antenati. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY SETTLE IT is Simone's own death act in GIARRE MORTI (he was 44 in 1820, so he died between 1820 and about 1860), which would name his parents and his spouse; or Marianna's, which an Italian death index files under her MAIDEN name, so D and M must both be checked. Giarre's Morti run to about 147 volumes and none is banked.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Morti 1820–1860, swept whole for SIMONE NICOTRA (39 of 41 years)
scope: Giarre (Catania), Archivio di Stato di Catania. All forty-one Giarre death years from 1820 to 1860 were banked in one window on 11 October 2026 — forty-one ark-to-container lookups without a 403, the longest run this archive has had. Twenty-three are read: 1820–1842. The target is SIMONE NICOTRA, «di anni quarantaquattro, contadino» in Giarre Nati 1820 atto 198, so born about 1776; and his wife MARIANNA, written DAIDONE there and MUSUMECI in Rosario Nicotra's 1890 death act. A death act names the deceased's PARENTS and the SPOUSE, which is both halves of that question at once.
result: SIMONE NICOTRA IS IN NO GIARRE DEATH TAVOLA FROM 1820 TO 1860. Forty of the forty-one years are read (1854 excepted, below). He was forty-four in April 1820 by his daughter's birth act, so he would have been eighty-four by 1860: HE DIED AFTER 1860, OR HE DIED SOMEWHERE ELSE. Neither has a Marianna Musumeci appeared in any M section, which is read in the same view as N at no extra cost. WHAT THE SWEEP FOUND INSTEAD IS HOW CROWDED THE SURNAME WAS — NINE NICOTRA HOUSEHOLDS OF GIARRE, each a couple the index itself names: SIMONE x DAIDONE MARIANNA (1820, burying a daughter five weeks after the same couple registered another in the birth register — confirmed twice, independently); SALVADORE x SPINA ROSA (1820); MARIANO x SPINA SANTA (1821); FRANCESCO x FRESTA ANNA (1827); ALFIO x PAPPALARDO ROSA (1831, 1836) and then ALFIO HIMSELF in 1842, «BRACCIALE, figlio di NICOTRA GIUSEPPE e PENNISI LEONARDA», which adds GIUSEPPE x LEONARDA PENNISI above him; D.r D. ALFIO x CONSOLI D. ANTONINA (1847); D. FERDINANDO x RUBBIERO CONCETTA (1856); and GIUSEPPE x COCO CARMELA (1859). Nine Nicotra fathers in one small town is exactly the situation in which a shared surname proves nothing, and NONE OF THEM IS ATTACHED TO ANYBODY. TWO FINDINGS WORTH CARRYING OUT OF THIS. (1) 1842 PROVES THE INSTRUMENT: a death act here really does write down the deceased's parents, which is why this was the right book. (2) 1847 CLOSED A LOOP THE ARCHIVE ALREADY HAD OPEN: «NICOTRA SALVATORE, figlio di NICOTRA D.r D. ALFIO e CONSOL D. ANTONINA», died 3 August 1847 — which is why that couple, who registered a son Salvadore in November 1846, registered a SECOND Salvatore in January 1848. The first died at nine months. METHOD, FOR WHOEVER COMES NEXT. 1850 IS NOT READ, AND AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS ROW SAID IT WAS. Segnatura 16098, the Giarre deposit (container w99kPgr, label «Giarre > 1850»), is scanned short — it ends at act 167 against its own closing line of 176, with no index at all. This row then claimed the Tavola was recovered from «the duplicate», segnatura 16480, container 57Vre6X. IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE. ITS MANIFEST LABEL READS «MACCHIA > 1850». MACCHIA IS A DIFFERENT COMUNE, and the Tavola read there — with its hamlet and trade columns — BELONGS TO MACCHIA'S DEAD, NOT GIARRE'S. The claim that «the two-deposit rule has actually paid here» was false: there is no second Giarre deposit for 1850. SO THIS SWEEP IS THIRTY-NINE OF FORTY-ONE YEARS, NOT FORTY — 1850 AND 1854 ARE BOTH UNREAD. Whatever names were taken from that Tavola are Macchia people and must not be read as Giarre ones. 1854 IS NOT READ AND IS NOT A NEGATIVE: two years' indexes are interleaved in its container's tail — image 123's left page is a clean 1854 M section and its FACING page carries an N heading with one line dated 1856, «NICOTRA SEBASTIANO, ACI REALE, BRACCIALE» — and the 1854 N section was never reached. That stray man is unplaced too, and I checked rather than assumed: Giarre's own 1855 and 1856 Tavole do not contain him. THE D SECTION, FOR DAIDONE, HAS NOT BEEN READ IN ANY YEAR — an Italian death index files a married woman under her MAIDEN name, so Marianna could be waiting under D in a year counted here as read. That gap is recorded rather than assumed.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Morti 1820–1860, the D section swept for DAIDONE (39 of 39 years)
scope: Giarre (Catania). A SECOND PASS OVER A SWEEP ALREADY CALLED DONE, to close a gap the first pass created and recorded. The Nicotra sweep read the M and N sections, which sit side by side, so MUSUMECI came free; the D section sits pages earlier and was skipped in every one of the forty years. An Italian death index files a married woman under her MAIDEN name, so MARIANNA DAIDONE — wife of Simone Nicotra by Giarre Nati 1820 atto 198, born about 1780 — could have been sitting under D in a year already counted as read. All thirty-nine readable years were reopened at their D section.
result: THERE IS NO DAIDONE IN ANY GIARRE DEATH TAVOLA FROM 1820 TO 1860. What is there instead is D'Urso, D'Angelo, D'Agata, Di Bella, Di Stefano, Di Mauro, D'Aquino, Denaro, Di Dio and a great many foundlings given invented surnames. EIGHT YEARS RULE D BLANK ALTOGETHER — 1823, 1825, 1827, 1828, 1830, 1832, 1841 and 1847 — and 1841 is the cleanest of all, because that volume gives every letter its own page and D is an empty sheet carrying nothing but its heading. 1845 and 1860 hold a DAMIANI, which is the nearest thing in forty years and is not the same name. SO THE WHOLE RESULT, ACROSS THREE SURNAMES: neither SIMONE NICOTRA nor his wife MARIANNA — looked for under NICOTRA, under DAIDONE and under MUSUMECI — died at Giarre between 1820 and 1860. He was forty-four in April 1820 and would have been eighty-four at the end of the span. THEY DIED AFTER 1860, OR THEY DIED SOMEWHERE ELSE. Rosario was at Mascali by 1841, where his son Giovanni was born, so MASCALI'S OWN DEATH REGISTERS BEFORE 1873 are the obvious next place; this archive has read Mascali Morti only from 1873. ONE YEAR IS STILL UNREAD IN EVERY LETTER: 1854, whose container interleaves two years' indexes in its tail.

source: Antenati — MASCALI Morti 1820–1872, swept for NICOTRA and DAIDONE (51 of 52 years)
scope: Mascali (Catania). Forty years of GIARRE deaths hold neither Simone Nicotra nor his wife Marianna, under Nicotra, Daidone or Musumeci. Rosario was at Mascali from 1841 and died there in 1890, so MASCALI BEFORE 1873 was the obvious next place; this archive had read Mascali Morti only from 1873. Every pre-1873 Morti container was resolved from its ark and its Tavola read. THE MASCALI RULE APPLIES THROUGHOUT: these sections are NOT reliably alphabetical, so a missing letter proves nothing unless the whole Tavola is read heading to heading, and that is how 1820-1865 were read. FROM 1866 THE FORMAT CHANGES COMPLETELY — the post-unification volumes carry an «Indice annuale» ORDERED BY FORENAME, so there is no D page or N page at all and the only way to search is to read the SURNAME COLUMN of every entry under every letter. That change silently breaks a surname-based search and is the single most important methodological finding here.
result: FIFTY-ONE OF FIFTY-TWO YEARS READ. 1844 HAS NO MORTI VOLUME IN ANY SERIES. ONE YEAR IS NOT ESTABLISHED: 1831 is faded past reading — Antenati stamps the plates «Faded Document», the ink is gone in places, and the run from M into P where an N section would sit holds one entry (no. 74) whose surname cannot be read. NO DUPLICATE DEPOSIT EXISTS for Mascali 1831-1833, so the two-deposit rule that rescued Giarre Morti 1850 has nothing to offer; 1831 stays open rather than being counted as a negative. 1869's index is partly under a black archive mask and is NOT claimed exhaustive. NEITHER SIMONE NICOTRA NOR MARIANNA DAIDONE IS AMONG THE DEAD OF MASCALI IN THESE YEARS. But the surnames are emphatically here, which Giarre could not show: SIX NICOTRA DECEDENTS — 1848 atto 118 SALVADORE of Giarre, son of Alfio x Pappalardo Rosa; 1851 atto 108 ANGELA, daughter of Alfio x Previtera Santa; 1862 atto 48 CARMELA, daughter of Giovanni; 1868 atto 28 CARMELA; 1869 atto 63 ALFIO; 1872 atto 80 MARIA or MADDALENA, daughter of Gaetano. AND THE FIRST DAIDONE DECEDENT FOUND ANYWHERE IN THIS PROJECT: 1841 atto 6, ANGELA DAJDONE, aged fifty, «NATA IN MASCALI», daughter of the late Giuseppe, against forty years of Giarre that hold not one Daidone of any kind. EVERY NICOTRA WAS VERIFIED BY NATIVE-SCALE CROP, because NICOLOSI and NUCIFORA both appear in these same Tavole and are the known look-alike trap; 1862 and 1868 each spell NICOLOSI within two lines of the NICOTRA, which is as good a control as the record can give. ALSO CONFIRMED IN PASSING: in 1872 the physical DUPLICATA card lies across the opening and MOVES BETWEEN EXPOSURES — covering the left page in one and the right in the next — so reading both exposures gives the whole opening. That is this archive's own recorded rule and it is what made 1872 readable.

source: Antenati — MASCALI Morti 1869 atto 63, ALFIO NICOTRA read in the original
scope: Mascali. The index of 1869 names an ALFIO NICOTRA, and «Nicotra Alfio» is the father named in BOTH earlier Mascali Nicotra death acts — Salvadore 1848 atto 118 and Angela 1851 atto 108. A death act names the deceased's OWN parents, so this act reaches a generation ABOVE the two decedents and potentially alongside Simone. The act was read in the original and by native-scale region crops.
result: ALFIO NICOTRA DIED AT MASCALI ON 13 MAY 1869, AGED SEVENTY-THREE — so born about 1796 — «di professione lavorante, NATO IN GIARRE e domiciliato in questo comune, FIGLIO DEL FU GIUSEPPE E DELLA FU CATERINA [surname], MORTA IN GIARRE». Declarants Gioacchino Lo Po fu Antonino, 45, becchino, and Antonio Rossi fu Leonardo, 60, lavorante, both illiterate. SO A GIARRE-BORN NICOTRA WHO DIED AT MASCALI, AND HIS FATHER WAS GIUSEPPE NICOTRA OF GIARRE. Simone Nicotra was born about 1776 and Alfio about 1796, so GIUSEPPE IS OF SIMONE'S OWN GENERATION and a brother or close kinsman is the natural reading. THAT IS NOT PROVED AND IS NOT CLAIMED. TWO THINGS HONESTLY NOT ESTABLISHED. FIRST, in the ACT BODY the surname is written in a looser hand and NICOTRA CANNOT BE SEPARATED FROM NICOLOSI with confidence; the INDEX entry is unambiguous and crisp, so the index reading is what is recorded and the body is flagged. SECOND, the mother's surname is ILLEGIBLE — it may be Pennisi, Podarsi or Pedara. Giarre holds a «Giuseppe Nicotra x Pennisi Leonarda» household, but that wife's forename is LEONARDA and this one is CATERINA, so IT IS NOT A MATCH on present evidence and must not be written up as one.

source: Antenati — MASCALI Morti 1828 atti 49 and 103, the Tomarchio-Nicotra and Bassi-Dajdone households
scope: Mascali. The 1828 Tavola names a NICOTRA and a DAJDONE as MOTHERS — the first trace of either surname at Mascali. Both children's death acts were read in the original to place the women.
result: ATTO 49, 14 June 1828: CATARINA TOMARCHIO, aged TWENTY-TWO so born about 1806, braccialiera, «FIGLIA DEL FU CARMELO e di MARIA NICOTRA DOMICILIATA ANCHE IVI» — so MARIA NICOTRA WAS A LIVING WIDOW AT MASCALI IN JUNE 1828. A child born about 1806 puts that marriage BEFORE civil registration began in 1820, so the marriage act is PARISH-ONLY and not on Antenati. ATTO 103, 15 November 1828: SUOR MARGHERITA BASSI, A NUN, aged THIRTY-THREE so born about 1795, «CIVILE POSSIDENTE», «FIGLIA DEL FU D. DOMENICO e di D.a SANTA DAJDONE DOMICILIATA IN QUESTO COMUNE» — so DONNA SANTA DAJDONE WAS A LIVING WIDOW AT MASCALI IN NOVEMBER 1828. The «D.» and «D.a» are DON and DONNA: this is a titled, propertied family. BOTH WOMEN ARE OF SIMONE AND MARIANNA'S OWN GENERATION, not the next one down — Maria Nicotra born perhaps 1780-85, Santa Dajdone perhaps 1770-75. NEITHER WIDOW EVER APPEARS AS A DECEDENT: the whole of Mascali Morti to 1872 was swept for them afterwards and they are not in it. A SISTER OF MARIANNA IS PLAUSIBLE FOR SANTA DAJDONE AND IS NOT PROVED.

source: Antenati — MASCALI Morti 1831, the one year of the sweep that cannot be read
scope: Mascali. The 1820-1872 Morti sweep for NICOTRA and DAIDONE read fifty-one of its fifty-two years. 1831 is the exception. Antenati stamps these plates «Faded Document» and the ink really is gone in places; read at native 2319px and by region crops the Tavola gives G, L, M then P, R, S, T, and the run from M into P — exactly where an N section would sit — holds one entry, no. 74, whose surname cannot be resolved.
result: NOT ESTABLISHED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED AS A NEGATIVE. NO DUPLICATE DEPOSIT EXISTS: Mascali has a single Morti deposit for 1831, 1832 and 1833 (Stato civile della restaurazione 16894, 16895, 16896), and the only other Mascali series on Antenati is «Deputazione del Regno», which is 1714-1752 Riveli di anime e di terre and not register copies at all. So the two-deposit rule that rescued GIARRE Morti 1850 has nothing to offer here. What would settle it is the Archivio di Stato di Catania's own holding, or a parish copy.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Morti 1842 atto 189 read in the original: ALFIO NICOTRA, and the archive's own inference tested
scope: Giarre. The Giarre Morti sweep recorded «ALFIO x PAPPALARDO ROSA (1831, 1836) and then ALFIO HIMSELF in 1842». THAT IDENTIFICATION WAS AN INFERENCE FROM THE TAVOLA, never checked against the act, and it mattered because the Mascali sweep had just produced a SECOND Alfio Nicotra — Mascali Morti 1869 atto 63, born Giarre about 1796, son of a Giuseppe and a CATERINA. If the 1842 man were a different Alfio, the Rosa Pappalardo husband could have survived, remarried, and BE the Mascali man. The act was read to settle it.
result: THE INFERENCE HOLDS, AND THE ACT SAYS MORE THAN THE TAVOLA DID. Act 189, 18 December 1842, declared by Nicolo Russo, 51, becchino, and Giuseppe Trovatello, 40, becchino: died on 16 December «nella Casa di sua abitazione ALFIO NICOTRA D'ANNI SETTANTA, SPOSO DI ROSA PAPPALARDO, nato in Giarre, di professione BRACCIALE, domiciliato ivi, FIGLIO DI FU GIUSEPPE e di FU LEONARDA PENNISI». SO THE 1842 MAN IS THE ROSA PAPPALARDO HUSBAND, confirmed by the act and not by the surname. HE WAS BORN ABOUT 1772 — the age word is cramped and SIXTY cannot be absolutely excluded, which would put him at 1782; either reading places him IN SIMONE NICOTRA'S OWN GENERATION, Simone being born about 1776. AND THEREFORE THERE ARE TWO DISTINCT ALFIO NICOTRAS, both Giarre-born, both sons of a GIUSEPPE, dying twenty-seven years and one comune apart: ALFIO A, born about 1772, husband of ROSA PAPPALARDO, son of Giuseppe x LEONARDA PENNISI, dead at Giarre in 1842; and ALFIO B, born about 1796, father of the 1851 Mascali Angela by SANTA PREVITERA, son of Giuseppe x CATERINA, dead at Mascali in 1869. THEY CANNOT BE THE SAME MAN AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME HOUSEHOLD. WHAT IT OPENS: Alfio A's parents, GIUSEPPE NICOTRA and LEONARDA PENNISI, stand a full generation ABOVE Simone and both were dead by December 1842. If Simone is their son too, that is Simone's parentage found. NOT PROVED, and the Giarre Morti sweep of 1820-1860 contains no Giuseppe Nicotra as a decedent, so Giuseppe probably died before civil registration began in 1820 and is parish-only. LEONARDA PENNISI, however, would be filed under PENNISI in a Giarre death Tavola, and she died at some point before 1842 — that is a readable target this archive has never looked for.

source: Antenati — data/giarre-arks.tsv holds 321 MACCHIA registers filed as Giarre, and one of them was read as Giarre
scope: Giarre / Macchia (Catania). While resolving containers for a Giarre Morti sweep after 1860, a manifest label read «Macchia» where the ark list said Giarre. Every manifest carries its own comune in its label, so the list was tested against it.
result: THE ARK LIST IS MIXED. data/giarre-arks.tsv holds 808 rows; 321 OF THEM ARE MACCHIA REGISTERS, NOT GIARRE. The discriminator is exact: every ark beginning an_ua1999 is Macchia and every other ark is Giarre. EIGHT WERE CHECKED AGAINST THEIR MANIFEST LABELS, spread across fifty years — an_ua19993187 (1821), an_ua19993197 (1831), an_ua19993209 (1842), an_ua19993218 (1850), an_ua19993231 (1862), an_ua19994600 (1866), an_ua19994601 (1867), an_ua19994603 (1871) — AND ALL EIGHT SAY MACCHIA. The two groups also have ZERO OVERLAPPING SEGNATURA VALUES, so they are two distinct archival series and not a duplicate deposit of one. MACCHIA IS ITS OWN COMUNE, later absorbed into Giarre, and its registers were never a second witness to Giarre's. WHAT THIS BREAKS. build_coverage.py and build_holdings.py both map the whole file to «Giarre», so this archive's holdings and coverage pages CREDIT GIARRE WITH 321 REGISTERS IT DOES NOT HOLD and show Macchia nowhere at all. THE FIX IS MECHANICAL AND IS NOT APPLIED HERE: split the an_ua1999 rows into data/macchia-arks.tsv and register that file in both tools. It changes two visible pages, so it is left for a deliberate decision rather than done at the tail of a long session.

source: Antenati — MACCHIA Morti 1862, read for NICOTRA and DAIDONE (and it is Macchia, not Giarre)
scope: Macchia (Catania), a comune later absorbed into Giarre. This volume was opened believing it to be GIARRE Morti 1862, because data/giarre-arks.tsv files it as Giarre; its own manifest label reads «Macchia > 1862» and its Patria column names Macchia, Milo and Dagala, which are Macchia's own hamlets. Read as part of the hunt for Simone Nicotra, who would have been eighty-six in 1862.
result: A SURNAME-ORDER TAVOLA WITH PATRIA AND BOTH PARENTS, read whole at the two sections that matter. There is nothing to search but the acts themselves — seventy-four openings — so 1866 IS NOT SWEPT AND IS NOT A NEGATIVE. source: Antenati — GIARRE Matrimoni 1845–1860 swept for a NICOTRA GROOM (15 of 16 years)
scope: Giarre. THE REASON THIS WAS THE RIGHT BOOK: a marriage act names BOTH sets of parents, so a son of SIMONE NICOTRA marrying here would be written «figlio di Simone Nicotra e Marianna Daidone» — Simone attached, not inferred. Simone's daughter Rosaria was born in 1820, so sons born 1805-1825 would marry roughly 1830-1855. The 1820s were already read across three comuni; 1830-1844 were already read at Giarre; THIS IS THE REMAINING GAP. All sixteen containers were resolved from their arks and EVERY ONE VERIFIED AGAINST ITS OWN MANIFEST LABEL as Giarre before reading, after this archive's Macchia lesson. These Tavole index by the GROOM'S SURNAME ONLY, so a bride of the name never appears under her own letter.
result: NO NICOTRA GROOM IN ANY OF THE FIFTEEN READABLE YEARS. The N sections hold NICOLOSI(1846), NICIFORA(1847), NEO(1849), NERI and NUCIFORA(1850), NICOSIA(1852), NUCIFORA(1855), NICOLO(1857), NUCIFORA(1859) — the whole family of look-alikes and not one Nicotra. FOUR YEARS RULE N BLANK OR HAVE NO N SECTION AT ALL: 1845 and 1848 rule it empty (1848 rules O empty too), and 1853, 1856, 1858 and 1860 run M straight into O or P. TWO FINDINGS WORTH MORE THAN THE NEGATIVE. FIRST, 1851 IS ORDERED BY THE GROOM'S FORENAME, not his surname — «Alfio Nucifora», «Domenico Calabrese», «Nunzio Torrisi» — so there is no N section at all and a surname search finds nothing while appearing to work. All 64 of its marriages were read down the surname column instead. That is the same trap Mascali springs from 1866, and it is now documented at Giarre fifteen years earlier. SECOND, 1857 WAS SETTLED BY THE ACT AND NOT BY THE INDEX: its single N entry reads «Nico?a» at native resolution and cannot be separated from NICOTRA by eye, so act 67 was found and read — «Mro SALVADORE NICOLO di anni TRENTUNO, nato in questo Comune, FIGLIO DI FU GIACOMO e di ANGELA GRASSO», marrying Venera Finocchiaro. «Grasso Angela» matches the Tavola's mother, so it is the same entry, and THE SURNAME IS NICOLO. ONE YEAR IS NOT SWEPT AND IS NOT A NEGATIVE: 1854 HAS NO TAVOLA AND NO INDEX OF ANY KIND — the volume closes with the Sindaco's certification of «SESSANTACINQUE atti di solenne promessa» and then a blank printed form under the archive's «Blank Page(s)» card. Searching it means reading all 65 acts. GIARRE IS THEREFORE BLIND IN BOTH SERIES FOR 1854, since Giarre Morti 1854 is also unread for an unrelated reason. WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE QUESTION: Simone Nicotra had no son who married at Giarre between 1845 and 1860, unless that son married in 1854.

source: Antenati — GIARRE Morti 1854: the Tavola mapped from its start, the D section read, and the N proved ABSENT
scope: Giarre. This year had been recorded as «opened and not safely read» because two years' indexes appeared interleaved in the container's tail, with the advice to try «the 1854 duplicate deposit». BOTH HALVES OF THAT NEEDED TESTING: the Macchia split of 11 October 2026 had just proved that Giarre's apparent duplicates are a different comune, and nobody had ever read the Tavola from its BEGINNING. Container Lme8WWa, 127 images, label verified «Giarre > 1854».
result: THE TAVOLA IS NOW FULLY MAPPED AND THE «INTERLEAVING» IS EXPLAINED. 1854 runs B and C on image 120, D, E and F on 121, G, I, L and the start of M on 122, and M COMPLETING ON 123'S LEFT PAGE at entry 224. THERE IT STOPS. Image 123's RIGHT page opens a different year — one N entry dated 2 GENNARO 1856 — and images 124 to 126 carry P, Q, R and onward with EVERY ENTRY DATED 1856. THE BINDER PUT 1856'S N-TO-Z RUN WHERE 1854'S BELONGS. So 1854 HAS NO N, O, P, Q, R, S, T, V OR Z AT ALL. The N section is NOT UNREAD; IT IS NOT IN THE VOLUME, and no re-reading will produce it. The only route to 1854's N is the acts themselves — at least 229 of them by the M section's own numbering. THE CLERK'S OWN CROSS-REFERENCE CONFIRMS THE READING: the C section on image 120 ends «SEGUE ALL'ULTIMA PAGINA», and image 127, the last page, duly carries the C overflow — so the volume's structure is deliberate and understood, not damaged. WHAT WAS GAINED. THE D SECTION HAD NEVER BEEN REACHED BY ANYONE AND IS NOW READ: D'AGATA Tommaso(66), D'MAURO Filippo(75), DEL PIZZO Rosario(91), with E ruled blank beneath. NO DAIDONE IN 1854. AND THE STRAY MAN IS PLACED AT LAST: «NICOTRA SEBASTIANO, ACI REALE, BRACCIALE» is ATTO 2 OF 1856, not an 1854 death — which is exactly why checking Giarre's 1855 and 1856 Tavole for him had failed to settle it, and why his act (Giarre Morti 1856 atto 2) is now a cheap and specific thing to read. THE ADVICE THIS ROW REPLACES WAS WRONG: there is no Giarre duplicate for 1854; segnatura 16485 / an_ua19993223 is MACCHIA.

source: Antenati — MACCHIA Morti 1821–1862 swept for SIMONE NICOTRA and MARIANNA DAIDONE (40 of 41 years)
scope: Macchia (Catania), Archivio di Stato di Catania. 45 Morti containers resolved from their arks and checked against their manifest labels; the N and D sections of every Tavola read, fifteen acts opened.
result: NO SIMONE NICOTRA AND NO MARIANNA DAIDONE AT MACCHIA IN ANY READ YEAR, 1822-1860 and 1862 (1821 has no Tavola and was not read; 1861 has no volume). WHAT TURNED UP IS A MILO NICOTRA FAMILY, never seen before: Macchia's hamlet of Milo holds at least four Nicotra households — SALVADORE (d. 1838) and ALFIO (d. 1843), brothers and sons of a CIRINO NICOTRA and a MARIA MELITA; a second SALVADORE with ANNA COSTA; CIRINO × ROSA RUSSO; GIACOMO × ANGELA GRASSO — recorded through child and adult deaths. The elder CIRINO, his sons' generation and Simone's are the same age and place, and NOTHING YET LINKS SIMONE TO THEM: the hypothesis is stated and not drawn. THREE TAVOLA FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING: the Tavola's hand renders Nicotra as NICOLOSI (1849), so a Nicolosi whose parents are a known Nicotra pair is opened, not dismissed; 1836 and 1837-39 Tavole are ordered by FORENAME in places; and Macchia files D'Agata under A, so a D section can be blank while the name is present. STILL OPEN: Macchia Morti 1866-1890, the births and marriages, and Simone's own death, which may lie in none of the registers Antenati holds.

source: Antenati — MACCHIA Morti 1866–1875 swept for SIMONE NICOTRA and MARIANNA DAIDONE (8 of 10 years; 1868-69 have no volume)
scope: Macchia (Catania), Italian-era death registers 1866, 1867, 1870-1875 (nine containers, the 1875 supplement included). Only 1872, 1874 and 1875 carry an annual index (1873's is ordered by forename); the rest were read act by act from the margin name.
result: NO SIMONE NICOTRA AND NO MARIANNA DAIDONE IN ANY OF THEM. Two Nicotra deaths, both at Milo in 1870: GIUSEPPE, about sixty, son of the late Alfio Nicotra and Lucia Bella (the Alfio of 1843), and ROSA, about forty, wife of Mariano Trovato and daughter of a late Salvadore Nicotra × Giuseppa Vitale who matches no Salvadore found. With 1821-1862 (earlier row) this closes Macchia Morti to 1875 except 1821 and the two absent years: Simone, born about 1776, would have been 99 in 1875 and Marianna 95, so THE DEATH SWEEP OF THE FOUR COMUNI THAT COULD HOLD THEM (Giarre, Mascali, Riposto, Macchia) IS NOW SUBSTANTIALLY COMPLETE AND THEY ARE NOT IN IT. What remains: the unread and absent years (Giarre 1850 and 1854 N, 1856-1865 and several others; Mascali 1831; Macchia 1821, 1868-69, 1861), a death in a comune never swept, or a death before 1820 when registration did not exist. STILL OPEN: Macchia Nati and Matrimoni, and the baptismal route for the elder Cirino Nicotra of Milo.

source: Antenati — MACCHIA Matrimoni 1821–1867 swept for a NICOTRA groom and for Simone and Marianna as parents (40 of 43 years)
scope: Macchia (Catania), 46 Matrimoni containers 1821-1867 (the 1841, 1850 and 1851 supplements included) resolved and checked against their manifest labels; the groom-indexed Tavola of each year read, and 15 acts opened.
result: NO MARRIAGE NAMES SIMONE NICOTRA OR MARIANNA DAIDONE, and no Nicotra groom of the age of a son of theirs turns up (1828's N is not in the volume; 1866-67 are only partly read; 1861 and 1863-65 and 1868-77 have no volume). WHAT TURNED UP: the Milo family, much better placed. CIRINO NICOTRA (b. c.1810, m. 1835 Rosa Russo) is the son of a SALVADORE × ALFIA CANNAVÒ — almost certainly the Salvadore × Giuseppa Strano who died in 1838 — and the brother of the Rosario who died in 1834; FILIPPO (b. c.1827, m. 1851 the widow Giuseppa Nicolosi) and GAETANO (b. c.1835) are that Salvadore's sons by Giuseppa Strano; GIUSEPPE (b. c.1810) married three times (1841 Angela Torrisi, 1851 Maria Vasti, 1857 Francesca Giomingo); the Salvadore × Anna Costa daughters Caterina (m. 1851) and Maria (m. 1858) and the Alfio × Lucia Bella daughter Concetta (m. 1849) all married in; SEBASTIANA NICOTRA, a widow, turned up only in her daughter's act (1849); and a separate ANGELO NICOTRA × ANGELA COSTA household lived at SANT'ALFIO in 1855. GIACOMO NICOTRA × ANGELA GRASSO's marriage is in the 1825 Tavola (act not opened). NOTHING LINKS SIMONE. THE FACT THAT HAS CHANGED IS HOW MUCH OF THE MILO GENERATION OF SIMONE'S AGE IS NOW DOCUMENTED AND HOW LITTLE OF IT CONTAINS HIM: a man born about 1776 who lived in Sant'Alfio in 1820 and is in none of the death, marriage or (for Macchia, Giarre, Mascali, Riposto) civil registers swept, may have died or been recorded in a place or year not swept, or under a variant of the name; that is a possibility and not a finding. STILL OPEN: Macchia Nati and the 1866-67 acts, and the parish route.

source: Antenati — MACCHIA Nati 1822-1865 swept for Nicotra births and for Daidone (42 of 45 years; 1821, 1826 and 1830 have no Tavola)
scope: Macchia (Catania), 54 Nati containers 1821-1865 (supplements included) resolved and checked against their manifest labels; the child-indexed Tavola of each year read at N and D by four readers (one session, three delegated), and about 25 acts opened.
result: NO DAIDONE AND NO CHILD OF SIMONE AND MARIANNA IN ANY READ YEAR. THE MILO HOUSEHOLDS NOW HAVE THEIR CHILDREN, YEAR BY YEAR: Salvadore Nicotra × Giuseppa Strano (Maria 1822, Salvadore 1823, Maria 1828, Palma 1832, Gaetano 1834, and Filippo c.1827), Salvadore × Anna Costa (Caterina 1821, Maria 1824, Teresa 1836, Santo 1837, Concetta 1839), Giacomo × Angela Grasso (Giuseppa 1829, Filippa 1833, three daughters named Rosaria 1831-37), Cirino × Rosa Russo (Salvadore 1836, Rosaria 1837, Giuseppe 1840, Maria 1843, Mauro 1845, Salvadore 1848), Filippo × Giuseppa Nicolosi (Giuseppa 1851, Salvadore 1853, Carmela 1857), and Giuseppe × Vasti/Giomingo. Three new households: Ferdinando × Concetta Pappalardo of Macchia, Salvadore × Venera Finocchiaro of Macchia, and a younger Giuseppe × Filippa Cavallaro of Milo. A correction: the Maria Patti of the 1851 death act is almost certainly Maria VASTI. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS: ROSARIO NICOTRA × VENERA MORABITO, bracciale of Milo, four children 1850 (Giovanna), 1852 (Francesco), 1855 (Salvadore), 1857 (Angela). Giovanni Nicotra's 1872 marriage papers give his parents as Rosario Nicotra and Venera MURABITO; Morabito and Murabito are one surname, Venera's ages fit a son born about 1841, and the occupations match. It is a CANDIDATE: his declared ages (about 42-48) do not reach the «about ninety» of the Rosario of 1890, no Giovanni is in the Macchia births of 1841 or 1847, and none of the four acts names Rosario's parents. STILL OPEN: the 1890 Mascali death act's age and Venera's death, the Giarre or Mascali births that link Giovanni to a Rosario at Milo, and the Macchia births after 1865.
